fields.name: Fields of Wind (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Air

You force the wind to obey your command, lifting any number of willing creatures within 100 feet of you. Each affected creature gains a flying speed of 60 feet as long as it doesn't move more than 100 feet away from the spellcaster. If it does, the creature loses the flying speed and falls if it is still aloft, but it regains the flying speed if it enters within the spell's range again.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 30-foot-radius circle centered on you and deals 12d6 thunder damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 104 (Indie)

fields.name: Fire Collar (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Fire

You attempt to create a magical, non-burning collar of flames around the neck of a beast you can see within range. It must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw, or the collar forms around its neck and it is charmed for the duration. If you or creatures friendly to you are fighting it, it has advantage on the saving throw.
	While the creature is charmed, it understands your commands and will try to fulfill them to the best of its ability. You can give a simple command, such as attacking a creature or running in a direction, as a free action. Whether or not it carries out a more complex command depends on the creature's Intelligence and the judgment of the GM. If the creature completes the order and doesn't receive further instructions from you, it defends and preserves itself to the best of its ability.
	If you or an ally of yours deals damage to the creature, it can repeat the saving throw, ending the spell on a success.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell with a 5th-level spell slot, the duration is concentration, up to 10 minutes. When you use a 6th-level spell slot, the duration is concentration, up to 1 hour. When you use a spell slot of 7th level or higher, the duration is concentration, up to 8 hours.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals 7d6 fire damage plus 1d6 fire damage for each slot level above 4th.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 104 (Indie)

fields.name: Fire Crown (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Fire

You attempt to create a magical, non-burning crown of flames on the head of a humanoid creature you can see within range. It must make a Wisdom saving throw, and if it fails, the crown forms on its head and it is charmed for the duration. If any ally or friendly creature is fighting against the target, it has advantage on the saving throw.
	While the crown remains on the target, as long as it can clearly hear you, it will obey your commands to the best of its ability. You can give commands for simple actions, such as attacking a target or running in a direction, as a free action.
	If you want to give an order of the length of a sentence, you must spend a bonus action. If the creature completes the action and can no longer hear or receive new commands, it will use its action to defend and preserve itself as best as it can. If you or an ally of yours deals damage to the creature, it may repeat the saving throw, ending the spell on a success.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a 6th-level spell slot, the duration is concentration, up to 10 minutes. When you use a 7th-level spell slot, the duration is concentration, up to 1 hour. When you use a spell slot of 8th level or higher, the duration is concentration, up to 8 hours.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 30-foot cone and deals 8d6 fire damage plus 1d6 fire damage for each slot level above 5th.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 105 (Indie)

fields.name: Fire Dragon Transformation (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a red, gold, or brass dragon scale, which the spell consumes)
fields.text:
Element: Fire

You infuse flames into your body, transforming into a humanoid creature with draconic features. For the duration of the spell, your scales grant you an AC that cannot be less than 14 + your Constitution modifier, your senses grant you blindsight of 30 feet, your wings grant you a flying speed of 60 feet, and you become immune to fire damage but vulnerable to cold damage.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 45-foot cone, deals 11d6 fire damage and can be used as a bonus action.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 105 (Indie)

fields.name: Fire Essence (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Fire

You can create or manipulate fire to produce one of the following effects:

	• You create a magic flame in your hand, which can take any form but can't be larger than 1 cubic foot. You can absorb non-magical flames within a range of 60 feet, extinguishing 5 feet of them, and transforming the flame in your hand into a magical and harmless source of light that sheds bright light in a 10-foot radius and dim light for an additional 10 feet.

	• You can ignite an object or space up to 5 cubic feet in size, illuminating your surroundings. The flames can only be extinguished if you command them to do so or if they are covered by at least 1 liter of water from a magical source. You can create as many magic flames as you wish.

	• You can make the flames take on simple shapes, such as the vague form of a creature or object, and animate them as desired, providing a fun and useful way to create illusions or entertain others.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 105 (Indie)

fields.name: Fire Lobotomization (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (any translucent gem worth at least 500 gp)
fields.text:
Element: Fire

You point the gem at a creature you can see within range and cast a fiery-looking ray from your forehead, which pierces through obstacles and reaches the creature's mind. The creature must make an Intelligence saving throw. On a success, the creature falls unconscious and wakes up if it takes damage or if another creature uses an action to wake it. On a failure, the creature's Intelligence and Wisdom are reduced to 1. The affected creature can't cast spells, activate magic items, understand language, or communicate in any intelligible way, but it can still identify its friends, follow them, and protect them. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of its turns, and if it succeeds three times, it will overcome the effects of the spell. However, if it fails three times, including the first, it will be permanently affected by the spell.
	The effects of this spell can be ended by a heal, greater restoration, wish, or any similar spell or ability.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 45-foot cone and deals 12d6 fire damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 105 (Indie)

fields.name: Fire Shackles (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Fire

You attempt to create magical, non-burning chains around the limbs of a creature of your choice that you can see within range. It must make a Wisdom saving throw, and if it fails, the shackles form and it will be charmed for the duration. If an ally or friendly creature is fighting against the target, it has advantage on the saving throw.
	While the chains remain on the target, you have telepathic communication with it and always know where it is, even on another plane, and it will obey your commands to the best of its ability. You can give commands of simple courses of action, such as attacking a target or running in a direction, as a free action. If you want to give an order of a sentence length, you must use a bonus action. If the creature completes the action and receives no new commands, it will use the action to defend and preserve itself as best as it can.
	If you or one of your allies deals damage to the creature, it may repeat the saving throw, ending the spell on a success.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell with a 9th-level spell slot, the duration is concentration, up to 8 hours.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 60-foot line that is 5 feet wide and deals 12d6 fire damage plus 1d6 fire damage for each slot level above 8th.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 106 (Indie)

fields.name: Fireheart Bond (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Fire

You try to awaken the warmth of friendship within another person. Choose a humanoid that you can see within range and that can clearly see and hear you. It must make a Wisdom saving throw, and does so with advantage if you or your companions are fighting it. If it fails the saving throw, it is charmed by you until the spell ends or until you or your companions do anything harmful to it. The charmed creature regards you as a friendly acquaintance. When the spell ends, the creature knows it was charmed by you.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each slot level above 1st. The creatures must be within 30 feet of each other when you target them.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals fire damage, affects a 20-foot line that is 5 feet wide, and deals an extra 1d6 fire damage for each 2 slot levels above 1st.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 106 (Indie)

fields.name: Fissure (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Earth

You manipulate the earth, opening a fissure within range, starting at a point you can see. The fissure occupies a line 50 feet long and 10 feet wide. Within the line, a chasm opens up to a depth of 20 feet, and creatures within the area must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, they fall into the chasm. The terrain inside the fissure is considered difficult, and its walls are sandy, making any Strength (Athletics) check to climb it to be rolled against your Spell Save DC.
	Starting at your next turn, you can close the fissure as an action. Creatures still inside it must make a Constitution saving throw, taking 6d12 force damage on a failure, or half as much on a success. Until the start of your next turn after closing the fissure, it is not fully sealed, and a creature trapped inside the fissure has total cover but is restrained and can use their action to make a Strength saving throw. On a success, they can use their full movement to try to climb out, ending the condition when they leave the fissure, but for every 1 foot of movement required, they must spend an additional 1 foot, emerging in an adjacent space to the fissure if the movement is sufficient. On a failure, they cannot move. At the start of the next turn after the fissure is closed, it is fully sealed, and all creatures still inside it are incapacitated and have their movement reduced to 0. Creatures with burrowing movement are immune to the effects of closing the fissure. The fissure closes automatically at the end of the spell or if you lose concentration.

Elemental Flux: With your next elemental surge, you stomp the ground. All creatures in a 20-foot radius circle centered on you must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take 10d6 bludgeoning damage and be knocked prone.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 106 (Indie)

fields.name: Flame Body (HB)
Flame Hammer (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a ruby worth at least 400 gp)
fields.classes: School: Evocation, Touch Spells, Elementalist (Tanares), Elementalist (Tanares) (Fire)
fields.text:
Element: Fire

You infuse your hands, or the hands of a willing creature you touch, with a mystical blue flame, creating a magical hammer that deals 3d10 fire damage per attack. The creature wielding the hammer is considered proficient with it and can use their Strength, Dexterity, or Wisdom modifier for attack and damage rolls. As a bonus action, the creature can suppress or release the weapon at any time for the duration of the spell.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 30-foot cone and deals 11d6 fire damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 107 (Indie)

fields.name: Flame Weapon (HB)
fields.classes: School: Evocation, Touch Spells, Elementalist (Tanares), Elementalist (Tanares) (Fire)
fields.text:
Element: Fire

You touch a willing creature and for the duration of the spell, all of the creature's natural and wielded weapons are considered magical and deal an extra 1d6 fire damage.

At Higher Levels: When you use a 5th or 6th level spell slot, the extra damage increases to 2d6, and if you use a 7th level or higher spell slot, the extra damage becomes 3d6.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 20-foot line that is 5 feet wide and deals 5d6 fire damage plus 1d6 fire damage for each slot level above 3rd.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 107 (Indie)

fields.name: Flames of Adoration and Fear (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a dragon scale, chromatic for fear or metallic for adoration)
fields.text:
Element: Fire

You ignite your spirit with flames, emitting an aura that generates adoration or fear in a specific type of creature around you. You choose a type of intelligent creature as the target of this spell, and all of those within range are affected according to the chosen aura as follows:

Frightful Aura: This aura causes the chosen creatures within range to feel fear. Each creature of the chosen type that starts its turn or enters the aura must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become frightened of you for the duration of the spell. A creature that succeeds the saving throw is immune to the effect for 1 minute. While frightened, the creature uses its movement to reach the safest place possible where it cannot see you and is out of range. When it is out of range and can no longer see you, the creature is no longer frightened. If the creature re-enters the range or can see you again, it becomes frightened once more. Whenever a creature takes damage, it can repeat the saving throw, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Adoration Aura: This aura causes all chosen creatures within range to adore you as a revered entity. Each creature of the chosen type that starts its turn or enters the aura must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become charmed by you for the spell's duration. A creature that succeeds the saving throw is immune to the effect for 1 minute. A charmed creature approaches you as closely as possible and will adore you in the best way its culture or customs would venerate a figure of respect, as determined by the GM. Whenever a creature can no longer see you and is more than 60 feet away from you, it is free from the effect, but will become affected again if it sees you or is within 60 feet of you once more. If a creature takes damage, it can repeat the saving throw, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 45-foot cone and deals 12d6 fire damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 107 (Indie)

fields.name: Flames of Fear (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Fire

All creatures you choose within the spell's range and that can see you must make a Charisma saving throw. A target automatically succeeds the saving throw if it is immune to the frightened condition. On a failure, the target is affected by the spell. Until the end of the spell's duration, you can, as a bonus action, specify a location that is not occupied by a creature where the creatures will believe that blazing flames are erupting, emitting extreme heat. At the start of their turns, each affected target within 30 feet of the chosen point must move away from the heat source at all its speed before taking any other actions. A creature that is forced to move by this effect may repeat the saving throw at the end of its turn, freeing itself from the effect on a success. A creature that does not move for any reason remains frightened until it moves away. A creature will not walk to a location that is obviously a mortal danger, such as a cliff, but it may provoke opportunity attacks during its movements.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals 7d6 fire damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 107 (Indie)

fields.name: Flames of Heart (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Fire

You kindle the flames of courage in the hearts of all willing creatures that you can see and that can see you within the spell's range. For the duration, affected creatures have resistance to psychic damage, are immune to being charmed or frightened, and have advantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws. It also dispels any ongoing effects of being charmed or frightened.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 45-foot cone and deals 14d6 fire damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 108 (Indie)

fields.name: Flames of Heroism (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Fire

You ignite the fighting spirit of up to five willing creatures within the spell's range. An affected creature becomes immune to be frightened, gains a bonus of 1d4 on its attack rolls, and its armed and unarmed attacks become magical and cause an extra 1d6 fire damage.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a 6th-level or 7th-level spell slot, the range of the spell increases to 60 feet and the extra damage increases to 1d8. If you use an 8th-level or higher spell slot, the range of the spell increases to 90 feet and the extra damage increases to 1d10.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 20-foot radius circle centered on you and deals 8d6 fire damage plus 1d6 fire damage for each slot level above 5th.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 108 (Indie)

fields.name: Flames of Leadership (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Fire

You amplify the flames of leadership within you. For the duration of the spell, you have advantage on Charisma (Persuasion, Deception, and Intimidation) checks. Once during the spell's duration, you can give a one-word simple command to a creature within 60 feet, which must make a Wisdom saving throw, following the command on a failure. The command has no effect if the target is undead, if it doesn't understand your language, or if your command is directly harmful to it. After following the command, all other effects of the spell end. Some typical commands and their effects follow. You might issue a command other than one described here. If you do so, the GM determines how the target behaves. If the target can't follow your command, the spell ends.

Approach: The target moves toward you by the shortest and most direct route, ending its turn if it moves within 5 feet of you.

Drop: The target drops whatever it is holding and then ends its turn.

Flee: The target spends its turn moving away from you by the fastest available means.

Grovel: The target falls prone and then ends its turn.

Halt: The target doesn't move and takes no actions. A flying creature stays aloft, provided that it is able to do so. If it must move to stay aloft, it flies the minimum distance needed to remain in the air.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a 4th-level spell slot or higher, for the duration of the spell, you gain an extra use of the command for every 2 slot levels above 2nd that you use. The bonus to ability checks granted by this spell only ends when the last use of the command is used.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals 2d6 fire damage plus 1d6 fire damage for each slot level above 2nd.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 108 (Indie)

fields.name: Flash (Tanares) (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Fire

You swiftly clap your hands together, producing a strong flash of light with a 15-foot radius. All creatures within the spell's range and that can see the light must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, the creature will be blinded until the end of its next turn.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 10-foot radius circle centered on you, deals fire damage, and on the damage roll, consider any result of 1 or 2 as a 3.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 108 (Indie)

fields.name: Fluid Sense (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Water

By invoking the power of water, you are able to sense all living creatures and water elementals. You know the exact location of these creatures within range, and you can determine its species and if the creature is losing liquid (such as from bleeding, for example).

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 40-foot line that is 5 feet wide and deals 8d6 cold damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 108 (Indie)

fields.name: Focused Blast (HB)
fields.time: 1 reaction, which you take when you or a creature you can see within 60 feet of you becomes a target of a spell or effect that deals damage in an area
fields.text:
Element: Fire

You focus the energy of an area spell or effect that deals damage onto a single creature of your choice that was originally targeted by that spell or effect. The chosen creature must be within range of the spell or effect, and you must have a clear line of sight to it.
	The chosen creature takes an additional 1d6 damage of the same type as the original spell or effect, and the DC of any saving throws it makes against the spell or effect increases by 2.
	For example, if a fireball is about to detonate in a 20-foot radius around you and other creatures, you can use focused blast to redirect the full force of the fireball only to that creature. The target makes its saving throw as usual, but the original DC is increased by 2. If it fails, it takes an additional 1d6 of fire damage.
	You must have a clear line of sight to both the caster and the chosen creature. If you do not have a clear line of sight to either of these, the spell fails. This spell does not allow you to target a creature that was not in the original affected area.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 20-foot line that is 5 feet wide and deals 5d6 fire damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 109 (Indie)

fields.name: Focused Image (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Air

You create the image of an object, a creature, or some other visible phenomenon that is no larger than a 5-foot cube. This image appears at a spot that you can see within range and lasts for the duration. Only one chosen creature can sense this image and it seems completely real, including sounds, smells, and temperature appropriate to the thing depicted. You can't create sufficient heat or cold to cause damage, a sound loud enough to deal thunder damage or deafen a creature, or a smell that might sicken a creature.
	As long as you are within range of the illusion, you can use your action to cause the image to move to any other spot within range. As the image changes location, you can alter its appearance so that its movements appear natural for the image. For example, if you create an image of a creature and move it, you can alter the image so that it appears to be walking. Similarly, you can cause the illusion to make different sounds at different times, even making it carry on a conversation, for example.
	Physical interaction with the image reveals it to be an illusion, because things can pass through it. A creature that uses its action to examine the image can determine that it is an illusion with a successful Intelligence (Investigation)
check against your spell save DC. If a creature discerns the illusion for what it is, the creature can see through the image, and its other sensory qualities become faint to the creature.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, the spell lasts until dispelled, without requiring your concentration.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals 2d6 thunder damage plus 1d6 thunder damage for each slot level above 2nd.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 109 (Indie)

fields.name: Force of Wind (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Air

You create a strong wind from a point of your choice within range, forming a 60-foot long, 10-foot wide, and 20-foot tall line that blows in the direction of your choice for the duration. Each creature that starts its turn in the line must make a Strength saving throw or be pushed 15 feet in the direction of the wind and be knocked prone. Any creature standing in the line must spend an extra 2 feet of movement for every 1 foot it moves in the direction against the wind.
	The gust also disperses gas or vapor and extinguishes unprotected flames such as candles or torches in the area, while protected flames like lanterns dance wildly and have a 50%
chance of being extinguished.
	As a bonus action, you can change the direction of the wind or move the starting point of the wind.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 20-foot line that is 5 feet wide and deals 7d6 thunder damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 109 (Indie)

fields.name: Gale Gate (HB)
Granite Body (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a one-inch cube of granite)
fields.classes: School: Evocation, Touch Spells, Elementalist (Tanares), Elementalist (Tanares) (Earth)

fields.name: Gravity Seal (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a diamond worth at least 1,000 gp, which the spell consumes)
fields.text:
Element: Earth

You greatly increase the effect of gravity on a creature that you can see within range. The target creature is not prevented from taking actions, but using its movement, an action, or a bonus action requires a herculean effort, causing the creature to take 2d12 force damage and suffer one level of exhaustion for each action taken. In addition, attacks that deal bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage deal double damage to the creature.
	For the duration of the spell, at the start of each turn, the target creature may make a Strength saving throw, and if successful, it is free from the effects of the spell for that turn, but it still retains all exhaustion levels gained from previous failures. If the target's Strength score is 10 or less, it automatically fails the saving throw.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 45-foot cone and deals 14d6 acid damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 110 (Indie)

fields.name: Ground Wave (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Earth

You stomp the ground with incredible force, creating a massive shockwave that travels through the earth. Each creature in contact with the ground and within a 90-foot cone from you is pushed back in the opposite direction from you. They are pushed away until they leave the area of the spell.
	Each creature that is moved in this way must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, they fall prone and take 1d8 bludgeoning damage for every 10 feet they were pushed away. Creatures that succeed on the saving throw take half damage and are not knocked prone, but still are pushed away from you.

Elemental Flux: With your next elemental surge, you stomp the ground. All creatures in a 30-foot radius circle centered on you must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw taking 11d6 bludgeoning damage and being knocked prone on a failed save.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 110 (Indie)

fields.name: Gust Fantasy (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a pinch of rice powder)
fields.text:
Element: Air

You alter the appearance of a number of willing creatures equal to your Wisdom modifier, all of which must be within a 30-foot-radius sphere centered on a point of your choice within range. You decide how they look, including height, weight, facial features, tone of voice, hair length, coloring, and distinctive features, if any. They can resemble a member of another species, although none of their statistics change, but you can choose one racial trait to grant to the transformed creatures. They also cannot resemble a creature of a different size, and their basic shape remains the same; if you are bipedal, you cannot use this spell to become quadrupedal, for example. At any time during the spell's duration, the affected creature can use its action to revert its appearance to normal, ending the effect on it.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each slot level above 3rd.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals 5d6 thunder damage plus 1d6 thunder damage for each slot level above 3rd.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 111 (Indie)

fields.name: Harm Liberation (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a cup of water)
fields.classes: School: Evocation, Touch Spells, Elementalist (Tanares), Elementalist (Tanares) (Water)
fields.text:
Element: Water

You purify a creature you touch, removing all afflictions upon it. If the creature is asleep, it awakens, and all wounds are removed, restoring the target to full hit points. The water also removes any diseases, curses, or conditions of charmed, frightened, paralyzed, or stunned. In addition, if the target is in the prone condition, it may use its reaction to stand up. Also, the creature gains 70 temporary hit points for 1 minute.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 60-foot line that is 5 feet wide and deals 14d6 cold damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 111 (Indie)

fields.name: Healing Blast (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Water

You unleash a burst of pure water at an allied creature, restoring 9d8 hit points and removing the charmed, blinded, or deafened conditions.

At Higher Levels: When you cast using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, you increase the healing value by 1d8 for each level above 4th.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals 7d6 cold damage plus 1d6 cold damage for each slot level above 4th.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 111 (Indie)

fields.name: Healing Drops (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Water

You harness the regenerative properties of the water element to restore 1d6 + Wisdom modifier hit points to a creature that you can see within range. If the amount healed exceeds the creature's maximum hit points, the excess value can be converted into temporary hit points for the next minute.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals cold damage, and on the damage roll, consider any result of 1 or 2 as 3.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 111 (Indie)

fields.name: Healing Rain (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Water

You create a magical rain at a point of your choice within range, healing all creatures of your choice in a 20-foot cube centered on that point. You heal 4d8 hit points, which you can distribute as you see fit among the creatures in the area (minimum of 0 hit points per creature). This spell has no effect on undead or constructs.
	All creatures within the area of the spell become wet as if they have been bathed with 3 gallons of water.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the healing increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 3rd.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals 5d6 cold damage plus 1d6 cold damage for each slot level above 3rd.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 111 (Indie)

fields.name: Healing Storm (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Water

You manifest a large storm infused with the healing energy of water essence, covering an area of 20-foot cube. This storm heals up to 50 hit points, distributed as you wish among creatures within the area. Creatures healed by this spell are also cured of non-magical diseases and the blinded, deafened, and poisoned conditions at the cost of 5 hit points per effect from the storm's healing limit.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 30-foot cone and deals 8d6 cold damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 111 (Indie)

fields.name: Healing Tempest (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Water

You conjure a great storm imbued with the healing power of water essence, covering a 20-foot cube area. When you cast the spell and at the beginning of each turn for the duration, the storm heals up to 100 hit points, distributed as you choose among creatures within the area. Creatures healed by this spell can also be cured of non-magical diseases and the blinded, deafened, and poisoned conditions at the cost of 10 hit points from the healing limit of the storm per effect. This magic does not affect undead or constructs. Each of your turns, the amount of healing power of the tempest returns to 100 during the spell's duration.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 45-foot cone and deals 14d6 cold damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 112 (Indie)

fields.name: Heat Vision (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a ruby worth at least 10 gp)
fields.classes: School: Evocation, Touch Spells, Elementalist (Tanares), Elementalist (Tanares) (Fire)
fields.text:
Element: Fire

You touch a willing creature to grant it the ability to see heat and discern objects and creatures through this vision. For the duration, that creature has darkvision out to a range of 90 feet.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals 2d6 fire damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 112 (Indie)

fields.name: Hell Dragon Eye (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Fire

Upon casting this spell, your eyes glow with an eerie light. At the start of each of your turns, you may choose any number of creatures you can see. Each one must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become frightened of you. A creature frightened in this way must use its actions to move as far away from you as possible via the safest available route, unless it can't move. If it moves to a spot that is at least 60 feet away from you, it is no longer frightened. If the creature can't move, it must make another Wisdom saving throw at the end of its turn. On a failed save, it falls unconscious until it takes damage or until someone uses an action to awake it. A creature that was already frightened by this spell and is targeted again, it makes the saving throw with advantage.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 30-foot cone and deals 10d6 fire damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 112 (Indie)

fields.name: Hellfire Gaze (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a lump of coal)
fields.text:
Element: Fire

Your eyes convey the horrors of the creatures' worst nightmares. Each creature in a 30-foot cone must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or drop whatever it is holding and become frightened for the duration.
	While frightened by this spell, a creature must take the Dash action and move away from you by the safest available route on each of its turns, unless there is nowhere to move. If the creature ends its turn in a location where it doesn't have line of sight to you, the creature can make a Wisdom saving throw. On a successful save, the spell ends for that creature.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals 5d6 fire damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 112 (Indie)

fields.name: Holy Stream (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a cup of holy water)
fields.text:
Element: Water

You choose a creature within range and create a blessed water current from your hands that purifies it. You can remove up to four of the following afflictions that may be affecting the target: one level of exhaustion, blinded, charmed, deafened, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, one curse (including the target's attunement to a cursed magic item), any reduction in one of the target's ability scores, and an effect that reduces the target's maximum hit points.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 30-foot cone and deals 10d6 cold damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 113 (Indie)

fields.name: Homing Spark (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Lightning

You condense the energy of lightning in your hand and gain the ability to shoot lightning bolts at your enemies. With a bonus action, you can make a ranged spell attack and shoot a bolt of lightning at a creature within range. On a hit, the creature takes 10d8 lightning damage and must make a Constitution saving throw, becoming stunned for the next minute on a failed save. A stunned creature can repeat the Constitution saving throw at the end of each of its turns to end the condition. Attacks against a creature wearing metal armor, wielding metal weapons, or carrying large metal objects are made with advantage.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 80-foot line that is 5 feet wide and deals 14d6 lightning damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 113 (Indie)

fields.name: Hurricane (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Air

You can accelerate the wind to create a tornado that affects a cylinder with a 60-foot radius and 200-foot height centered on a point of your choice within range. Creatures that start their turn or enter the area, except for the caster and three creatures of their choice, must make a Strength saving throw or be sucked into the tornado.
	Flying creatures in the area must make the Strength saving throw with disadvantage, and flying creatures within 30 feet of the tornado must make a Strength saving throw to avoid being sucked into it. Unattended objects and items are also sucked into the tornado. Flying creatures can make another Strength saving throw, with disadvantage, at the beginning of their turn, freeing themselves from the effects until the start of their next turn.
	Creatures that are sucked into the tornado are pulled towards the center of the cylinder and lifted 40 feet in the air each turn. They are trapped in the tornado for the duration, considered incapacitated with a speed of 0.
	Buildings in the area take 20 points of bludgeoning damage at the start of your turns. If their hit points are reduced to 0, they are turned into debris and also sucked into the tornado.
	When the spell ends, each creature and object that was caught in the tornado is thrown 100 feet away in a random direction. To determine the direction, roll a d8 and assign a direction to each die face.
	If a creature is thrown in the same direction as debris from a building, it must make a Dexterity saving throw to avoid being crushed under the rubble. A creature hit by debris takes 5d6 bludgeoning damage.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 30-foot cone and deals 11d6 thunder damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 113 (Indie)

fields.name: Ignite Seal (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (gold, copper and ruby dust of a total value of at least 1,000 gp, which the spell consumes)
fields.classes: School: Evocation, Touch Spells, Elementalist (Tanares), Elementalist (Tanares) (Fire)
fields.text:
Element: Fire

You carefully create a powerful glyph on a surface, which can be a wall, table, throne, book cover, shield, etc., as long as it has a surface area of 1 foot in diameter. If you choose a surface that conceals the glyph, the spell will not take effect.
	The glyph is apparent and bright and clearly magical. While you cast the spell, you must set a trigger that you desire for the glyph's effect, such as touching or stepping on the glyph or the approach of a certain type of creature within 5 feet of it.
	When the glyph is activated, choose one of the following effects:

Disintegration: The glyph destroys the object or location where it was placed, heating it to the point of disintegrating everything within a 10-foot radius around it. A creature that touches the object or is in the area being disintegrated must make a Constitution saving throw, reducing its hit points to 0 and turning to dust on a failure or taking 6d8 radiant damage and 6d8 fire damage on a success.

Self-Destruction: The glyph self-destructs in a powerful explosion. All creatures within a 60-foot radius must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking 40d6 fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

Eternal Heat: The glyph emits a lot of heat. For the next 1001 days, any creature that starts its turn or enters a space within 30 feet of the glyph takes 4d8 fire damage, and creatures that are beyond these 30 feet but within 60 feet of the glyph must make a Constitution saving throw, taking 2d8 fire damage on a failure.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 45-foot cone and deals 14d6 fire damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 113 (Indie)

fields.name: Inner Fire (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Fire

You ignite the inner flames of a number of willing creatures within range, up to your Wisdom modifier. The affected creatures, which may include yourself, become immune to the frightened condition and any unarmed or melee weapon attacks they make deal an additional 1d4 fire damage.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals fire damage, and on the damage roll, consider any result of 1 or 2 as a 3.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 114 (Indie)

fields.name: Intertwining Roots (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Plant

Roots sprout from the ground, grabbing onto creatures within a 20-foot square centered on a point within range. For the duration, these roots turn the area into difficult terrain.
	A creature that enters or starts its turn in the area and fails a Strength saving throw is restrained until the end of the spell. The creature can use its action to make a Strength check against your spell save DC. On a success, it frees itself. When the spell ends, the conjured roots vanish.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals poison damage and requires a Constitution saving throw.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 114 (Indie)

fields.name: Lava Floor (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Lava

You unleash a dangerous spell that covers a 30-foot square area with a thin layer of lava, making it difficult terrain. Any creature that enters or starts its turn in the area must make a Constitution saving throw or suffer the consequences.4
	On a failed save, the creature takes 3d6 fire damage and has its walking speed, or any other speed that relies on contact with the ground, halved for a minute or until it takes an action to cool its feet outside the area. On a successful save, the creature takes half damage and avoids the speed reduction.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 10-foot-radius circle centered on you. All creatures in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw. Targets take 7d6 fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 114 (Indie)

fields.name: Leaf in the Wind (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Air

With a whisper, you surround yourself with the energy of Air, becoming one with the wind. For the spell's duration, you can move with incredible speed and agility, allowing you to use the Dash or Disengage action as a bonus action.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals thunder damage, and on the damage roll, consider every 1 or 2 as a 3.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 114 (Indie)

fields.name: Lesser Link (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Spirit

You create a spiritual connection with up to 3 willing creatures within range. For the duration of the spell, while a connected creature is within 15 feet of another, they have telepathic communication and you can use a reaction to grant advantage on an attack roll or saving throw of a connected creature within range.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals force damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 114 (Indie)

fields.name: Life Back (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a flask of holy water, which the spell consumes)
fields.classes: School: Transmutation, Touch Spells, Elementalist (Tanares), Elementalist (Tanares) (Water)
fields.text:
Element: Water

You purify the body of a dead creature with sacred waters, resurrecting the creature. The creature cannot have been dead for more than 10 days and revives with 1 hit point, free of any curses or conditions (except for exhaustion, which only recovers 1 level) that affected it at the time of its death. This spell does not restore lost parts and does not affect undead or constructs, or creatures whose soul does not want to resurrect, or creatures that have died from old age.

Elemental Flux: You can imbue your next elemental surge into the revived creature, which gains 5d8 temporary hit points lasting for 8 hours.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 114 (Indie)

fields.name: Life Swap (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Water

You forge a powerful connection between two willing creatures of your choice within range, causing them to instantly swap their current hit points and maximum hit points. If a creature's hit points drop to 0 as a result of the swap, that creature falls unconscious and begins dying.
	In addition to the hit point swap, the two creatures can choose to exchange any of the following effects, provided both creatures agree:

Condition Swap: Choose one of the following conditions: blinded, deafened, frightened, paralyzed, poisoned, or stunned. If one of the creatures is currently affected by the chosen condition, that creature is cured of the condition and the other creature becomes affected by it. This exchange lasts until the spell ends, at which point the conditions return to the originally affected creature.

Skill Swap: The two creatures choose one skill, tool, or language proficiency each and exchange the chosen proficiency for the duration of the spell.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the duration of the condition swap and skill swap increases by 1 extra hour for each slot level above 3rd.

Elemental Flux: If used for the duration of the spell, but before any other spell is cast, your next elemental surge deals 5d6 cold damage or grants 5d6 temporary hit points to creatures of your choice within the area of effect.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 114 (Indie)

fields.name: Life Synchronization (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Water

You synchronize the energy fluids of 4 willing creatures, which you can see within range, to heal them. You can transfer any amount of hit points between them, as long as each one has at least 1 hit point and does not exceed their maximum hit points. At the end of the synchronization (hit point transfer), you heal an additional 2d8 hit points from each of the creatures that have transferred hit points (taken damage or regained hit points). Undead and constructs are not affected by this spell.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 30-foot cone and deals 8d6 cold damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 115 (Indie)

fields.name: Lightning Arrester (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Lightning

You energize a target creature, forcing it to make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the creature becomes restrained and vulnerable to lightning damage for the duration of the spell. The restrained creature can use an action to make another Constitution saving throw, and if it succeeds, it breaks free from the restraint.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals lightning damage and affects a 30-foot line that is 5 feet wide.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 115 (Indie)

fields.name: Lightning Burst (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a pair of magnets)
fields.text:
Element: Lightning

You empower up to six willing creatures within range, imbuing them with the power of lightning. Until the spell ends, the targets gain the following benefits:

	• Their speed is doubled.
	• They gain a +2 bonus to their AC.
	• They have advantage on Dexterity and Strength saving throws.
	• Their melee attacks deal an extra 1d8 lightning damage.
	• They gain an additional action on each of their turns, which can only be used to take the Attack action (one weapon attack only), Dash, Disengage, Hide, or Use an Object action.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 50-foot line that is 5 feet wide and deals 11d6 lightning damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 115 (Indie)

fields.name: Lightning Displacement (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Lightning

You gain the ability to teleport up to your speed, but every 5 feet of distance teleported spends 5 feet of your speed for the current turn (you must have at least 10 feet of movement remaining for the spell to work). You must teleport to a destination within your line of sight. For example, you could teleport to the top of a wall, but not to a point in mid-air unless you have a means of flight. When you teleport, you leave behind a trail of lightning that damages any creatures in its path.
	All creatures in a line between your starting point and your destination must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, they take 5d8 lightning damage. On a successful save, they take half as much damage.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 50-foot line that is 5 feet wide and deals 8d6 lightning damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 115 (Indie)

fields.name: Lightning Tunnel (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a piece of light fabric)
fields.text:
Element: Lightning

You weave together strands of lightning into an invisible tunnel that can be up to 120 feet long and 5 feet in diameter. The tunnel remains stationary once created and lasts for the duration of the spell.
	Each round, the first creature or object that enters one end of the tunnel becomes an invisible and silent electrical charge that instantly travels through the tunnel to the other end, reforming in its original form. Creatures and objects that pass through the sides of the tunnel take no damage and are unaffected by the spell.
	However, when a creature is transported through the tunnel, any other creatures standing inside the tunnel's area take 2d6 lightning damage as the energy arcs through them. This damage has no visible source, and creatures that are transported through the tunnel are immune to it.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the length of the tunnel increases by 30 feet and the diameter increases by 5 feet for each slot level above 3rd.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 30-foot line that is 5 feet wide and deals 5d6 acid damage plus 1d6 acid damage for each slot level above 3rd.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 115 (Indie)

fields.name: Lightning Wall (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a copper wand worth at least 30 gp)
fields.text:
Element: Lightning

You create a barrier that looks like a net of pure energy. The barrier does not need to be sustained and can float in the air. It occupies an area of 60 feet in length, 20 feet in height, and one inch in thickness. Any creature within the area where the barrier was created must make a Strength saving throw, suffering 3d8 lightning damage on a failure and being thrown 10 feet in a direction of your choice. On a successful save, the target takes only half the damage and is expelled into the nearest free space, as chosen by the affected creature.
	The barrier magnetically affects an area of 15 feet around it. Inside this area, attacks made with metal weapons have disadvantage, and creatures made of metal or wearing metal armor move at half speed (moving 1 foot costs 2 feet of speed).
	A creature can attempt to pass through the barrier but must succeed on a Strength saving throw. On a failure, it takes 3d8 lightning damage and is thrown back 10 feet in a prone condition. On a success, it takes half damage and passes through the barrier.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 50-foot line that is 5 feet wide and deals 10d6 lightning damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 116 (Indie)

fields.name: Made of Lava (HB)
fields.classes: School: Evocation, Touch Spells, Elementalist (Tanares), Elementalist (Tanares) (Lava)
fields.text:
Element: Lava

You encase a touched creature with a barrier of lava, shielding it from attacks. For the duration, the creature is resistant to fire and cold damage. If the creature takes bludgeoning, slashing, or piercing damage from a creature adjacent to it, the barrier spews lava at the attacking creature, which must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take 3d8 fire damage.
	Optionally, the creature protected by the barrier can take a reaction upon being hit by a melee attack to make the barrier explode, causing every creature within 15 feet, except itself, to make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, creatures hit by the barrier take 6d8 fire damage. After using this reaction, the spell ends.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 30-foot cone and deals 11d6 fire damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 116 (Indie)

fields.name: Magic Precipitation (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Water

You create a magical precipitation area in a 20-foot-radius, 30-foot-high cylinder centered on a point within range that you can see. Creatures within the rain area gain advantage on saving throws against spells and resistance to magical damage. Additionally, any spells that are in effect on the area or on creatures of your choice that are in or enter the area are dispelled.
	Furthermore, when a spell is cast within the area or affects any space within it, you can choose to absorb the magic to fuel the precipitation. The absorbed magic has no effect, and the precipitation then heals your chosen allied creatures within the rain for an amount of hit points equal to twice the level of the spell slot used to cast the absorbed spell. The healing effect of this magic does not affect undead or constructs.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 45-foot cone and deals 14d6 cold damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 116 (Indie)

fields.name: Magma armor (HB)
fields.classes: School: Evocation, Touch Spells, Elementalist (Tanares), Elementalist (Tanares) (Lava)
fields.text:
Element: Lava

You touch a willing creature wearing medium or heavy armor and enchant their armor with the heat of magma. For the duration, every time another creature hits the target of the spell with a melee attack, it must make a Dexterity saving throw or take 1d10 fire damage.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals 2d6 fire damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 116 (Indie)

fields.name: Magma Chamber Heat (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (an obsidian worth at least 1000 gp)
fields.text:
Element: Lava

You heat up a circular area with a 100-foot radius centered on a point within range. The temperature in this area becomes unbearable. Creatures that enter or start their turn within it must make a Constitution saving throw or take 4d8 fire damage, or half as much on a success. Flammable materials not carried or held burn up in an instant.
	In addition, creatures that start and end their turn within the area must make another Constitution saving throw or suffer a level of exhaustion. Creatures wearing heavy armor make this saving throw with disadvantage.
	Creatures immune to fire are immune to the effects of this spell, and creatures resistant to fire automatically pass the saving throws.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 45-foot cone and deals 12d6 fire damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 117 (Indie)

fields.name: Magma Glow (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a piece of charcoal)
fields.classes: School: Evocation, Touch Spells, Elementalist (Tanares), Elementalist (Tanares) (Lava)
fields.text:
Element: Lava

You touch an object, causing it to emit a faint glow that is imperceptible in bright light and difficult to notice in dim light conditions. The object can be any item (magical or not) of your choosing, weighing no more than 10 pounds.
	While the spell is active, you can sense the location of the object as long as it is within 240 feet of you, even if it is behind walls, doors, or other barriers. The location is communicated to you as a general sense of direction (e.g., "northwest") and distance (e.g., "close", "very far").
	You can dismiss the spell at any time as a bonus action, causing the glow to fade immediately.
	The DC to notice the glow is equal to your spell save DC. Only a creature specifically looking for the glow can use its action to make a Wisdom (Perception) check against this DC to notice the glow. The object can be hidden inside fabrics or other objects, making it impossible to directly see the glow, without hindering your ability to sense its location.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the weight limit of the object increases by 10 pounds for each slot level above 1st.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals fire damage and gains an extra 1d6 fire for each slot level above 1st.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 117 (Indie)

fields.name: Magma Servant (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a pinch of obsidian dust)
fields.text:
Element: Lava

You summon a lava spirit that appears in an unoccupied space within range. It takes physical form to serve you, using the stat block of an azer, but appearing as a humanoid creature made of magma.
	The magma servant is an ally and recognizes your allies as allies. It shares your initiative, acting immediately after you, but has its own turn. The magma servant will obey your commands to the best of its ability. You can give simple course of action commands, such as attacking a target or running in a direction, as a free action. If you want to give a command that requires a longer phrase, you must use a bonus action. If the creature completes the action and cannot hear or receive new commands, it will take the Dodge action to preserve itself to the best of its ability.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals 5d6 fire damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 117 (Indie)

fields.name: Mantle of Water (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a drop of water)
fields.text:
Element: Water

You surround a target creature within range with a thin layer of clean water, granting it the ability to breathe underwater and a swimming speed of 40 feet. While the spell lasts, the creature gains the following benefits:

	• Immunity to the effects of non-magical fire, gasses and liquids, including harmful acids, poisons and smokes.

	• You have advantage on saving throws made against harmful magic gasses (such as cloudkill and stinking cloud effects, and the breath weapons of some dragons).

	• Resistance to fire and acid damage.

	• Immunity to being grappled and restrained.

The water mantle continuously replenishes the water the creature breathes and is covered in, filtering out harmful substances.
	In addition, the creature can use a bonus action to end the spell and unleash a water gust attack against a creature within 60 feet. The water gust requires a ranged spell attack roll and deals 3d10 bludgeoning damage on a hit.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals 7d6 cold damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 118 (Indie)

fields.name: Marble Skin (HB)
fields.classes: School: Evocation, Touch Spells, Elementalist (Tanares), Elementalist (Tanares) (Earth)
fields.text:
Element: Earth

You touch a creature and a seismic wave emanates from your fingers, enveloping it and imposing a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, the creature is restrained and its skin begins to turn to marble. On a success, the creature is unaffected. A creature with its skin turned to marble must make a Constitution saving throw at the end of each of its turns. If the creature accumulates three successes, it is free from the condition and the spell ends. If it accumulates three failures
(including the initial one), the creature becomes petrified.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 30-foot cone and deals 10d6 acid damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 118 (Indie)

fields.name: Mass Curse of Flames (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Fire

All creatures that you can see within range must make a Wisdom saving throw or be affected as if they were targets of the curse of flames spell cast with a 9th-level slot.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 30-foot radius circle centered on you and deals 14d6 fire damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 118 (Indie)

fields.name: Massive Inflammation (HB)
fields.components: V, M (bee's wings or a drop of honey)
fields.text:
Element: Fire

You ignite the spirit of a group of people by suggesting a course of action (limited to up to two sentences). You magically influence, at your discretion, a number of people equal to up to three times your proficiency bonus. The creatures must be able to see and hear you clearly and the suggestion must be phrased in a way that makes the course of action reasonable. Igniting them to do something against themselves, such as self-flagellation, negates the effects of the magic.
	Creatures that can't be charmed are immune to this effect.
	Each target must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, they pursue the course of action you described to the best of their ability.
	For the duration of the spell, the inflamed creatures are immune to the frightened condition and will continue to carry out the proposed course of action. If the activity can be completed in a shorter time, the spell ends when the target finishes what was requested.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a 7th-level spell slot, the duration is 10 days. When you use an 8th-level spell slot, the duration is 30 days. When you use a 9th-level spell slot, the duration is a year and a day.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge creates a burst around you, which affects a 20-foot radius circle centered on you and deals 10d6 fire damage plus 1d6 fire damage for each slot level above 6th.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 118 (Indie)

fields.name: Material Illusion (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Air

You choose the stat block of a non-spellcaster creature with a CR of up to 12, then you create a dense air replica of that creature, within an unoccupied space that you can see within the spell's range. The replica uses all the statistics of the creature it duplicates, except that any damage dealt by the replica is psychic damage. However, the replica can only damage or affect in other ways creatures that failed the saving throw. It acts on its own turn and on its own initiative, but you can control its course of action. If the replica's hit points are reduced to 0, the spell ends, and it immediately dissipates.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 45-foot cone and deals 14d6 thunder damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 118 (Indie)

fields.name: Melt Rock (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a drop of mercury)
fields.text:
Element: Lava

You choose an area of rock and change its internal heat, melting it into lava. You affect a 40-foot cube of rock within range. The lava flows and ignites any flammable materials it touches. A creature that touches the lava takes 2d8 fire damage.
	If a creature has a limb or body part covered by lava, it takes this damage at the end of its turns for the next minute or until it takes an action to remove the lava. A creature that is partially covered by lava has its speed halved and takes 4d8 fire damage for the next minute or until it takes an action to remove the lava. A creature that is completely covered by the lava is restrained, takes 8d8 fire damage, and requires 2 actions to completely remove the lava, but if it spends only 1 action, it is still considered to be partially covered by lava.

At Higher Levels: When you use a spell slot of 6th level or higher, you melt an extra 20-foot cube of rock per level above 5th.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 30-foot cone and deals 8d6 fire damage plus 1d6 fire damage for each slot above 5th.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 119 (Indie)

fields.name: Metal Barrier (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a pure metal ingot worth at least 100 gp)
fields.text:
Element: Earth

You hold the piece of metal used in this spell and it disintegrates into metallic sand, swirling around a willing creature within range of the spell, granting them protection. A creature enveloped in this protection gains resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage, is considered to have half cover, and when subjected to a Dexterity saving throw to take half damage from an effect, they take no damage on a success.
	Once during the duration, as a bonus action, you can change the target of the spell to another willing creature within range and at least 30 feet from the original target.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 40-foot line that is 5 feet wide and deals 10d6 acid damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 119 (Indie)

fields.name: Mirage Mirror (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Air

You conjure a duplicate of yourself from the energy of the wind, which appears in an unoccupied space within the spell's range. The duplicate has an AC equal to yours and one hit point, and it performs saving throws and ability checks as it were you. The duplicate does not move, but any action you take can also be simulated by the duplicate at your choice. A creature can make a Wisdom (Perception) check against your spell save DC to realize that the duplicate is not real. The duplicate disappears if you use a bonus action to dismiss it, if you move more than 60 feet away from it, or when its hit points are reduced to 0.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals thunder damage, and on the damage roll, consider every 1 or 2 as a 3.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 119 (Indie)

fields.name: Mineral Sculpt (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Earth

You manipulate earth and rocks to create objects within range. If using fresh earth (sand, clay, and general soils), you can create a large or smaller object (contained within a 10-foot cube, or eight connected 5-foot cubes), such as statues, bridges, passages, pillars, doors, etc., as long as there is enough earth to do so. If using metal or solid rock,.you can create only a medium or smaller object (contained within a single 5-foot cube), such as a weapon, idol, crown, etc. The objects are usually solid, without gears or hinges, and generally of good quality. However, the quality of objects, such as jewelry, statues, or any that require artistic or professional knowledge, may vary depending on your proficiency or the availability of the right tools.

At Higher Levels: When you use a spell slot of 5th or 6th level, you can make a huge object of fresh earth (contained within a 15-foot cube, or twenty seven connected 5-foot cubes) or a large object of solid material (contained within a 10-foot cube, or eight connected 5-foot cubes). When you use a spell slot of 7th level or higher, you can mold a gargantuan object of fresh earth (contained within a 20-foot cube, or four connected 10-foot cubes, or sixty-four connected 5-foot cubes).

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 20-foot line that is 5 feet wide and deals 7d6 acid damage plus 1d6 acid damage for each slot level above 4th.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 119 (Indie)

fields.name: Mirror Object (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a small polished gemstone)
fields.classes: School: Evocation, Touch Spells, Elementalist (Tanares), Elementalist (Tanares) (Water)
fields.text:
Element: Water

You touch a non-magical object weighing no more than 5 pounds, causing its surface to become reflective like a mirror. During the spell's duration, the object captures all images and sounds within a 30-foot radius, as long as they are reflected on its mirrored surface.
	When the spell ends, the object reverts to its original state, and the captured images and sounds are retained, hidden within it. To access the captured images and sounds, the object must be submerged in any body of water large enough to completely cover it. Once the object is submerged, the captured images and sounds are displayed on the surface of the water and can be viewed as if you were on the location. The size of the water surface determines the size of the image, with a larger surface allowing for more details to be seen.
	The object can store the captured images and sounds for up to 1 year. However, once the object is submerged and the images and sounds are accessed, or if it is removed from the water before the end of it, the information is lost and cannot be recovered.
	The quality of the captured images and sounds depends on the quality of the object used as a mirror. Polished and well-maintained objects capture clearer and sharper images and sounds, while dirty and worn objects can produce blurred and distorted images and sounds.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the weight limit of the object increases by 5 pounds for each slot level above 2nd.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 20-foot line that is 5 feet wide and deals 2d6 cold damage plus 1d6 cold damage for each slot level above 2nd.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 119 (Indie)

fields.name: Mountain Crush (HB)
fields.classes: School: Evocation, Touch Spells, Elementalist (Tanares), Elementalist (Tanares) (Earth)
fields.text:
Element: Earth

You deliver a powerful shoulder strike to your target. Make a melee spell attack against it. On a hit, the creature becomes stunned for 1 minute. On a critical hit, the primary target is violently pushed back 15 feet and can hit a creature of your choice as a secondary target, provided it's in the same direction and range as the primary target was pushed. In this case, the secondary target is also stunned. Oozes are immune to this spell.
	Each stunned target must make a Constitution saving throw at the end of its turns. If they succeed, the stunned condition ends.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 45-foot cone and deals 12d6 acid damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 220 (Indie)

fields.name: Move like Air (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Air

You and a number of willing creatures equal to your Wisdom modifier that you can see within the spell's range have their speed doubled, gain a +2 bonus to their AC, have advantage on Dexterity saving throws, and gain an additional action on each of their turns. The action can only be used to take the Attack (one weapon attack only), Dash, Disengage, Hide, or Use an Object action.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 40-foot line that is 5 feet wide and deals 11d6 thunder damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 220 (Indie)

fields.name: Move Like Water (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Water

You shield a willing creature of your choice that you can see within range, with the energy of the water element. For the duration, the creature does not provoke opportunity attacks, regardless of the action or movement they perform.
	Additionally, it gains a +1 bonus to AC.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals cold damage, and on the damage roll, consider any result of 1 or 2 as 3.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 220 (Indie)

fields.name: Mystical Flux (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a drop of water)
fields.classes: School: Evocation, Touch Spells, Elementalist (Tanares), Elementalist (Tanares) (Water)
fields.text:
Element: Water

You touch another creature and send a wave of mystical energy to it, causing it to instantly recover a spell slot of the same level as this spell or lower. You can't use this spell on yourself.

At Higher Levels: When casting this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, it equally increases the spell slot level that can be recovered by the target.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 20-foot line that is 5 feet wide and deals 2d6 cold damage plus 1d6 cold damage for each slot level above 2nd.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 221 (Indie)

fields.name: Natural Stream (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a drop of holly water)
fields.text:
Element: Water

A stream of water purifies the creature touched by it. You can remove one condition afflicting the target between blinded, charmed, deafened, paralyzed and poisoned.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals 2d6 cold damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 121 (Indie)

fields.name: Overcharge Lightning (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a pair of magnets)
fields.text:
Element: Lightning

You discharge energy that affects the nervous system of all creatures of your choice in a 20-foot square within range. A creature in the area must make a Constitution saving throw, becoming paralyzed on a failure. On a successful save, the creature's nervous system is fatigued and on its next turn, it cannot use one of its actions, be it an action, bonus action, or movement. A paralyzed creature can make another saving throw at the end of its turns, ending the condition on a success but still being affected by the action restriction on its next turn. If your concentration is broken, paralyzed creatures are released but still suffer from the action restriction. A creature that has passed the action restriction is freed from the effects of the spell.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 80-foot line that is 5 feet wide and deals 12d6 lightning damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 121 (Indie)

fields.name: Overgrow (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Plant

You energize all your allies within a 30-foot-radius circle from a point of your choice within range with an aura of vitality. The aura grants each ally 4d8 temporary hit points, a bonus of +1 to their AC, and advantage on Strength and Constitution checks and saving throws for the next minute.
	If creatures are grappled, restrained, or poisoned and need to make a roll to escape the condition, they can use their reaction to make the check or saving throw at the moment you cast this spell.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals 7d6 poison damage and requires a Constitution saving throw.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 121 (Indie)

fields.name: Petrify Nerves (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a small, straight piece of iron)
fields.text:
Element: Earth

You freeze the nerves of a creature of your choice within range of the spell. The creature must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be paralyzed for the duration. This spell does not affect undead or constructs. An affected creature can make a saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each slot level above 5th. The creatures must be within 30 feet of each other when you target them.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 30-foot cone and deals 8d6 acid damage plus 1d6 acid damage for each slot level above 5th.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 121 (Indie)

fields.name: Pour the Past (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Water

You use the energy of the water to make it swirl counterclockwise and see the events that occurred in the location where you cast the spell. The manifested image shows the events that occurred within a 30-foot radius of the location where you cast the spell. You see all the events as if you were above the location observing them. You can quickly observe all events that occurred up to 1 year ago or choose a specific moment to observe and follow it for the duration of the spell. Talk to your GM to define what details are perceptible from your point of view and the way you witnessed the events unfold.

Elemental Flux: After the spell's duration, you can create an ice statue of a creature or object of up to medium size that you saw with your next elemental surge. The statue lasts 1 minute and then melts into snowflakes that disappear.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 121 (Indie)

fields.name: Primordial Pass (HB)
fields.classes: School: Evocation, Ritual Caster, Elementalist (Tanares), Elementalist (Tanares) (Air)
fields.text:
Element: Air

You create a bridge made of air that connects one point to another, provided there is no object obstructing the path between these points. When a creature enters this point, the winds carry them from one point to the other on gentle breezes. The crossing lasts only 1 minute and is completely safe, with air currents protecting creatures during the journey.
	The path can be used by both sides, but the path is only open in one direction at a time while the crossing is taking place.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 45-foot cone and deals 10d6 thunder damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 122 (Indie)

fields.name: Prodigium Duplication (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a small piece of clay)
fields.classes: School: Evocation, Touch Spells, Elementalist (Tanares), Elementalist (Tanares) (Earth)
fields.text:
Element: Earth

You touch a non-magical object weighing up to 10 pounds, causing it to briefly glow with an earthy light before splitting into a number of identical copies equal to twice your proficiency bonus (minimum of 4). Each copy has the same appearance, weight, and physical properties as the original object, including any markings or inscriptions.
	However, the copies created by this spell bear an unnatural aura that makes them immediately identifiable as magical constructs to anyone who inspects them closely. As a result, it is very difficult to use these copies to deceive others or pass them off as genuine items.
	The copies created by this spell last for 1 hour or until they are destroyed, at which point they crumble into a pile of dust. You can end the spell prematurely by using a bonus action to cause one or more copies to disappear.
	The copies created by this spell are mundane objects and do not possess any magical properties. Additionally, they cannot be used to create copies of items made of precious metals or gems, as their unique physical properties cannot be replicated by this spell.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the weight limit of the object increases by 10 pounds for each slot level above 2nd.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 20-foot line that is 5 feet wide and deals 2d6 acid damage plus 1d6 acid damage for each slot level above 2nd.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 122 (Indie)

fields.name: Purging Flames (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a drop of oil)
fields.text:
Element: Fire

You immolate a hostile undead or extraplanar creature (devil, demon, penumbral, etc.) that you can see within the range of the spell. The target creature must make a Charisma saving throw. On a success, nothing happens, but on a failure, it is consumed by flames and it is destroyed, leaving only ashes behind. If the target is an undead whose soul is trapped elsewhere (such as a lich and its phylactery or an undead created from a body whose soul was trapped), it must make a second Charisma saving throw. On a failure, it is immolated and destroyed. If the target is extraplanar, it returns to its home plane and must make another Charisma saving throw. On a failure, it is immolated and destroyed.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 60-foot line that is 5 feet wide and deals 14d6 fire damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 122 (Indie)

fields.name: Quicksand (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Earth

You transform a 30-foot-radius circular area, centered on a point within range, into quicksand. The area becomes difficult terrain and every creature within it at the time of casting, or that starts its turn or enters the area, must make a Strength saving throw. On the first failure, the creature begins to sink in the sand and becomes restrained. On the second failure, the restrained creature sinks even further, becoming incapacitated. On a third failure, the incapacitated creature sinks completely into the sand and becomes stunned. Each time a creature succeeds on a Strength saving throw, it regresses one step in the number of failures, becoming unburied if it reaches 0 failures.
	A creature that is completely buried by this spell cannot breathe, is under total cover, has disadvantage on Strength saving throws, and suffers 3d10 bludgeoning damage for each failure it has on Strength saving throws. Failures beyond the third are added to the number of failures.
	Another creature that is adjacent to a buried creature and is not under any effect of the spell can use an action to help dig out the buried creature. The creature must make a Strength ability check against your spell save DC. On a success, it frees the creature from the spell's effects, but on a failure, it is pulled into the area of effect and counts as having failed a Strength saving throw against the spell.
