A creature within the area of effect that tries to help another does so with disadvantage on the Strength check.
	When the spell ends, all creatures that are restrained suffer 3d10 bludgeoning damage, all creatures that are incapacitated suffer 6d10 bludgeoning damage, and all creatures that are stunned suffer 10d10 bludgeoning damage. Objects and creatures that are dead or die from the final damage remain buried, while surviving creatures are expelled from the ground.
	Objects that are not being held are automatically buried, and structures within the area suffer 30 bludgeoning damage when the spell is cast, and at the beginning of each turn that you maintain the spell.

Elemental Flux: With your next elemental surge, you stomp the ground. All creatures in a 30-foot-radius circle centered on you must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw, taking 14d6 bludgeoning damage and being knocked prone on a failed save. Each creature within the quicksand area that is hit by this elemental surge fails in the saving throw automatically, counting as a failure for the spell too.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 122 (Indie)

fields.name: Rally of Agility (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Air

Up to four willing creatures are surrounded by strong winds that assist their movements. While under this effect, the affected creatures have their Dexterity scores increased by 6
(up to a maximum of 26), and they have advantage on any attacks or ability checks that involve Dexterity.
	A creature under the effect of the spell is immune to the grappled, restrained, prone and paralyzed conditions. Additionally, attacks against the target are made with disadvantage.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 45-foot cone and deals 10d6 thunder damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 123 (Indie)

fields.name: Regenerating Cocoon (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Plant

You create a large flower at a location of your choice within range that can envelop a willing creature, up to Huge size, that is within 15 feet of it. The creature is immune to damage, has its movement reduced to 0, and is incapacitated while inside the flower. The creature can leave the flower at any time. While inside the flower, the creature is healed for 2d8 + its Wisdom modifier at the start of each of its turns. The creature also removes 1 level of exhaustion every 2 turns spent inside the flower and gets rid of one curse, disease, or poison for every 4 turns spent inside it. If the creature remains inside the flower for the full duration of the spell, it regains any lost limbs.
	The flower automatically dissipates, ending the spell's effects if the creature exits it, you lose concentration, or the flower's hit points are reduced to 0. The flower has an AC of 15, 80 hit points, is resistant to non-magical damage, and immune to poison damage.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 30-foot cone and deals 11d6 poison damage and requires a Constitution saving throw.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 123 (Indie)

fields.name: Regrowth (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (fruits, flowers, seeds, rare herbs, dragon parts and jewelry that weigh more than the target and are worth at least 25,000 gp, which the spell consumes)
fields.classes: School: Evocation, Touch Spells, Elementalist (Tanares), Elementalist (Tanares) (Plant)
fields.text:
Element: Plant

You touch a body or a body part that still exists of a creature that has been dead for no more than 500 years. The part of the creature and any material components turn into a seed that automatically sprouts into a plant, generating a bulb where the body of the creature is recreated and restored. After 8 hours, the bulb opens, and the creature is revived, healed of all wounds, any poisons removed, all diseases cured, and freed from any curses that afflicted it when it died. The spell fully restores the body, replacing missing parts.
	If the body of the creature no longer exists, the casting time doubles, and you must speak the creature's name, take an object that belonged to it, and, as part of this spell, bring its spirit, which will be mixed with the material components when forming the seed. If the spirit is not available, the spell fails, and no components are expended.
	The spell can even provide a new body if the original no longer exists. The creature then appears in an unoccupied space you choose within 5 feet of the plant.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge, instead of dealing damage, imbues the creature's body with an elemental soul, leaving it immune to diseases and curses for a number of days equal to 10d6 days.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 123 (Indie)

fields.name: Revert Life Flux (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a large bowl of holly water)
fields.classes: School: Evocation, Touch Spells, Elementalist (Tanares), Elementalist (Tanares) (Water)
fields.text:
Element: Water

You harness a sacred water flow to reverse a loss of life in a body, resurrecting the creature. The creature cannot have been dead for more than 100 years, cannot be an undead or construct, must have a soul available for return to the body, and cannot have died of old age.
	At the end of the spell, the target creature returns to life with all wounds healed, regaining any lost limbs and free of any conditions, but it receives 4 levels of exhaustion. Additionally, the resurrected creature returns free of any non-magical diseases or curses. Magical diseases and curses will resume their effects if they are not removed beforehand.
	The flow of magic is very heavy and until a long rest is finished, you will receive two levels of exhaustion and have a -4 reduction to all attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws.

Elemental Flux: With your next elemental surge, you imbue the creature targeted by this spell and yourself with elemental energy, granting both 6d8 temporary hit points that last for 10 hours.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 123 (Indie)

fields.name: River Protection (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Water

You surround a willing creature that you can see within range with the healing energy of life, protecting its body from harm. The target creature cannot be a construct or undead.
	The target regains 4d8 hit points and gains immunity to the blinded, charmed, frightened, paralyzed, and poisoned conditions for the duration of the spell. If the creature was already affected by any of these conditions before the spell was cast, the effects are suppressed (but not ended) until the spell ends.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 30-foot cone and deals 10d6 cold damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 124 (Indie)

fields.name: Rock Stubborn (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Earth

For the duration, a willing creature that you can see within range and while in contact with the earth or rock, gains resistance to lightning and psychic damage, and has advantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each slot level above 3rd. The creatures must be within 30 feet of each other when you target them.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals 5d6 acid damage plus 1d6 acid damage for each slot level above 3rd.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 124 (Indie)

fields.name: Sacred Fruits (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (seeds from 3 different trees)
fields.text:
Element: Plant

You plant the seeds and grow a small, glowing plant that produces four fruits. If not harvested within 1 hour, the fruits wither and disappear. Once harvested, the fruits last for 24 hours before disappearing.
	A creature that consumes one of the fruits can remove any curses or frightened conditions from itself, and for the next 24 hours, it is sufficiently nourished, it gains 2d10 temporary hit points, becomes immune to the poisoned and frightened conditions, and has advantage on Wisdom saving throws.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 7th level or higher, you create one additional fruit for each level above 6th.

Elemental Flux: With your next elemental surge, you imbue the fruits with elemental energy. Before eating a fruit, a creature must speak a magical word. If a creature eats a fruit without speaking the word, it must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes 7d6 poison damage and is poisoned for 24 hours. On a successful save, the creature takes half damage and gains no benefits from the spell.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 124 (Indie)

fields.name: Saving Seed (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Plant

You create a small plant that bears a single fruit the size of a cherry. If eaten, as a bonus action, the fruit serves as a full meal, instantly restores all of your hit points, and cures any disease, blindness, deafness, poisoning, and all levels of exhaustion. The magical fruit lasts for 3 days and disintegrates after this time.
	Due to the amount of energy expended in casting this spell, you need a recharge time and can only use this spell after 7 days.

Elemental Flux: With your next elemental surge, you imbue the fruit with elemental energy. Before eating the fruit, a creature must speak a magical word. If a creature eats the fruit without speaking the word, it must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes 10d6 poison damage and is poisoned for 10 days. On a successful save, the creature takes half damage and gains no benefits from the spell.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 124 (Indie)

fields.name: Scrape The Sky (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Earth

You create up to 4 pillars of 30 feet in height each occupying a 5-foot square space within the spell's range. A creature in the space where the pillar appears must make a Dexterity saving throw or be thrown 30 feet into the air, landing prone in an adjacent space to the pillar. If succeeded, the creature does not take damage but must choose an adjacent space to position itself.
	With a bonus action, for the next minute, you can topple the pillars in a direction of your choice, each occupying a 30-foot long and 5-foot wide line. All creatures within the line of the pillar's fall must make a Strength saving throw, taking 1d8 damage and becoming restrained on a failure. A restrained creature can use its action to make a Strength (Athletics) check against your spell save DC, freeing itself on a success. Huge or larger creatures are immune to this effect. If you do not topple the pillars, they will dissipate after 10 minutes.

Elemental Flux: With your next elemental surge, you stomp the ground. All creatures in a 20-foot radius circle centered on you must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw, taking 7d6 bludgeoning damage and being knocked prone on a failed save.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 124 (Indie)

fields.name: Seismic Quake (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a gem worth at least 100 gp, which the spell consumes)
fields.text:
Element: Earth

You take a gem in your hand that crumbles when using the spell. When its fragments touch the ground, you generate an earthquake with a radius of 120 feet and an epicenter of your choice within range, causing the entire area of effect to become difficult terrain. At the time of casting and at the beginning of each turn of a creature within the area, it must make a Dexterity saving throw, becoming prone on a failure. Creatures that are concentrating on other spells must also make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC, losing concentration on a failure.
	Structures within the area suffer 60 bludgeoning damage when you cast the spell, and at the beginning of each of your turns that you maintain concentration. If they reach 0 hit points, they collapse and may cause damage to creatures beneath them, at the GM's discretion.
	In addition, at the GM's choice, other effects may occur, such as fissures or shifting ground. When a fissure is formed, it can have a depth of 3d4x10 feet and a width of 1d4x5 feet. Creatures in the area of the fissure must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, they fall into the fissure, or choose one of the edges to remain on the surface on a success. When the ground shifts, at the GM's discretion, a block may rise or sink 1d4x10 feet, taking everything on it along and causing structures it cuts through to collapse.

Elemental Flux: With your next elemental surge, you stomp the ground. All creatures in a 30-foot-radius circle centered on you must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw, taking 14d6 bludgeoning damage and being knocked prone on a failed save.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 125 (Indie)

fields.name: Shield of Overlife (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Water

You create a thin layer of water over your body, making it impossible for a creature to perceive you except through magical means. This magical layer provides you with 60 temporary hit points.
	Whenever a creature attacks you in melee, your shield drains bodily fluids from the attacker, causing the creature to suffer 3d8 + your Wisdom modifier necrotic damage, and you add the same amount of temporary hit points to the pool generated by this spell.
	As a bonus action, you can make the shield drain a creature within 5 feet, causing 3d8 + your Wisdom modifier necrotic damage, and you gain the same amount of temporary hit points.
	The shield has no limit on temporary hit points and retains its temporary hit points for 1 hour after the spell ends.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 30-foot radius circle centered on you and deals 14d6 cold damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 125 (Indie)

fields.name: Skin of Embers (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a pinch of charcoal powder)
fields.text:
Element: Fire

You attempt to ignite the skin of a creature you can see within range of the spell. The target creature must have some type of skin or leather covering its body and, if so, must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, its skin or leather transforms into incandescent material like live coals. On a success, nothing happens.
	A creature with fiery skin gains resistance to fire damage and vulnerability to all other types of damage. It can move in extremely high temperature environments but suffers one point of exhaustion each turn it is in extremely cold temperatures (below 32 °F). Touching or coming into contact with this creature causes 1d6 fire damage and automatically ignites any flammable materials.
	The creature with ember skin can repeat the Constitution saving throw at the end of its turns, and if it succeeds three times, it is free from the effects. If you maintain concentration for 1 minute while the creature is under the effects of the spell, its skin will permanently be transformed into embers, making this effect permanent. This effect can be removed only by a wish or similar powerful spell.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 40-foot line that is 5 feet wide and deals 8d6 fire damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 126 (Indie)

fields.name: Sky Blessing (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a feather of an eagle)
fields.classes: School: Evocation, Touch Spells, Elementalist (Tanares), Elementalist (Tanares) (Air)
fields.text:
Element: Air

A touched willing creature receives the blessing of winds, acquiring exceptional speed. The creature gains a flying speed of 180 feet, becomes immune to being prone, has advantage on Dexterity ability checks and saving throws, ranged attacks against it have disadvantage, it does not provoke opportunity attacks when moving, and is not affected by any gas-related effects.
	In addition, the target can spend 5 feet of its movement to automatically escape non-magical restraints.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each slot level above 5th.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 30-foot cone and deals 8d6 thunder damage plus 1d6 thunder damage for each slot level above 5th.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 126 (Indie)

fields.name: Sky Walker (HB)
fields.text:
Type: Air

By casting this spell, you grant the ability to walk on the winds to a creature you touch, giving it a flying speed equal to its walking speed. At the end of the spell, a creature that is still in the air descends safely to the ground.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each slot level above 3rd.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals 5d6 thunder damage plus 1d6 thunder damage for each slot level above 2nd.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 126 (Indie)

fields.name: Spectral Vision (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Spirit

For the duration of the spell, you are able to see the spiritual aura of all creatures within sight, even when they are invisible. Each type of creature has a specific type of aura that you can see, but you cannot differentiate between them (e.g., an orc and a human have the same aura because they are both humanoids). Additionally, as a bonus action, you can focus on seeing the Ethereal Plane, gaining vision of it until the end of your next turn.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 20-foot line that is 5 feet wide and deals 2d6 force damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 126 (Indie)

fields.name: Speed Waltz (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Air

Three willing creatures you can see within range are propelled by the wind. You can move them up to 30 feet in any direction you choose. This movement ignores difficult terrain and does not provoke opportunity attacks, but if a creature is stopped in mid-air, it falls as normal and takes falling damage.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each slot level above 2nd.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 20-foot line that is 5 feet wide and deals 2d6 thunder damage plus 1d6 thunder damage for each slot level above 2nd.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 126 (Indie)

fields.name: Sphere of M'Cel (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a pearl worth at least 100 gp)
fields.text:
Element: Air

You expel all the air from a 30-foot radius sphere centered on a point within range, and the area remains airless for the duration. All creatures within the area at the time of casting who require air to breathe must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, they suffer one level of exhaustion, as the air is sucked out of their lungs.
	Furthermore, creatures inside the sphere are subject to the normal rules for suffocation. They can hold their breath for a number of minutes equal to 1 + their Constitution modifier
(minimum of 30 seconds), and then survive a number of rounds equal to their Constitution modifier (minimum of 1 round) before they drop to 0 hit points and begin dying.
	In addition, the airless area becomes difficult terrain for the duration of the spell, and any creature that starts its turn within the area or moves into it on its turn must make a Constitution saving throw, suffering one level of exhaustion on a failed save. Creatures within the area are considered deafened, and no sound can propagate within it.
	Additionally, creatures inside the sphere are immune to thunder damage, and no thunder damage can be caused inside the sphere.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, the radius of the sphere increases by 5 feet for each slot level above 5th.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 30-foot cone and deals 8d6 thunder damage plus 1d6 thunder damage for each slot level above 5th.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 127 (Indie)

fields.name: Spirit Form (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Spirit

You and up to five other willing creatures within range take a step on the border of the Ethereal Plane, entering the region that overlaps with the current plane. While on the border, you can move in any direction as if you had a flying speed equal to your walking speed. You can still see and hear the original plane, but everything appears grayed out and muffled, and you can't see anything beyond 60 feet.
	For the duration, as a bonus action, a creature under the effect can choose to move from the Ethereal Plane to the original plane and vice versa. The creature returns to the same mirrored location it was occupying on the plane it left (if it exits the Ethereal Plane in midair and without a flying speed, the creature will fall).
	While on the Ethereal Plane, you can only affect and be affected by other creatures on that plane. Creatures not on the Ethereal Plane cannot perceive you or interact with you, unless a special ability, magic item, or spell has given them the ability to do so.
	You can move through objects that are not on the Ethereal Plane, ignoring any objects and effects from the plane you originated from.
	When the spell ends, you and your allies return to the plane of origin in the same location you occupied at the time. If you occupy the same space as a solid object or creature when this happens, you will immediately be moved to the nearest unoccupied space that you can occupy and take force damage equal to twice the number of feet you were moved.
	This spell has no effect if you cast it while on the Ethereal Plane or a plane that does not border it, such as one of the Outer Planes.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 60-foot line that is 5 feet wide and deals 14d6 force damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 127 (Indie)

fields.name: Spiritual Air Beasts (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Air

You summon up to five air spirits that take the form of beasts with a challenge rating of 1 or lower. They appear in an unoccupied space that you can see within range. A spirit disappears when it reaches 0 hit points or when the spell ends. They are friendly to you and your companions. Roll initiative for each of them, which act on their own turns. They obey any verbal commands that you issue to them (no action required by you). If you issue no commands, they defend themselves against hostile creatures, but they take no other actions. The GM can provide the statistics of the beasts.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 20-foot-radius circle centered on you and deals 10d6 thunder damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 127 (Indie)

fields.name: Spiritual Fading (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Spirit

For the next minute, at the end of your turns, if you are not grappled, you can choose to enter the Ethereal Plane, or when already there, return to the Material Plane. When you return to the Material Plane, you choose an unoccupied space within 20 feet of where you disappeared to reappear.
	While on the Ethereal Plane, you can see and hear the Material Plane, which appears in shades of gray, and you can't see anything there that is more than 60 feet away. You can only interact with and be affected by other creatures on the Ethereal Plane. Creatures that are not on the Ethereal Plane cannot perceive you or interact with you unless they have any means to do so.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals 5d6 force damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 127 (Indie)

fields.name: Spiritual Flame (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (ruby dust worth at least 50 gp)
fields.classes: School: Evocation, Touch Spells, Elementalist (Tanares), Elementalist (Tanares) (Fire)
fields.text:
Element: Fire

A black, blue or red translucent flame, equivalent in brightness to a torch, springs forth from an object that you touch. The flame is clearly magic and creates no heat and doesn't use oxygen. A spiritual flame can be covered or hidden but not smothered or quenched.
	With the object in hand, you can end the spell as a bonus action to emit a burst of intense light in a 30-foot radius around you, blinding all creatures within that area for 1 minute unless they succeed on a Constitution saving throw.
	You can choose to cast this spell consuming the ruby dust. If you do, spiritual flame is permanent and you cannot end its effect.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 20-foot line that is 5 feet wide and deals 2d6 fire damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 128 (Indie)

fields.name: Spiritual Hex (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Spirit

You curse a creature within range, causing malevolent spirits to jinx its actions and turn its failures into catastrophes. For the duration of the spell, any time the target misses an attack, fails a saving throw, or fails an ability check, it suffers additional harm or negative effects. Whenever the target misses an attack roll or saving throw, it takes 3d8 necrotic damage. If the target fails an ability check, it suffers the worst possible negative consequence appropriate to the situation, as determined by the GM.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, the damage from the missed attack rolls and saving throws increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 4th.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals 7d6 necrotic damage plus 1d6 necrotic damage for each slot level above 4th.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 128 (Indie)

fields.name: Spiritual Immunity (HB)
fields.classes: School: Abjuration, Touch Spells, Elementalist (Tanares), Elementalist (Tanares) (Spirit)
fields.text:
Element: Spirit

For the duration, a willing creature you touch becomes immune to acid, cold, fire, lightning, necrotic, poison, psychic, and thunder damage.

At Higher Levels: If you cast this spell using a 9th-level spell slot, you can also affect an additional willing creature within 5 feet of the spell's initial target.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 60-foot line that is 5 feet wide and deals 12d6 force damage plus 1d6 force damage for each slot level above 8th.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 128 (Indie)

fields.name: Spiritual Travel (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a mithral key encrusted with gems worth at least 500 gp)
fields.text:
Element: Spirit

You and up to six willing creatures within range of are transported to another plane of existence. You must have an object that is linked to the destination plane, have previously been to the plane, or have one of the willing creatures have been to the plane. If you do not meet at least one of these requirements, all of you vanish for one round and then reappear in the same location in a stunned condition until the end of your next turn.
	You can also use this spell to send a creature from another plane back to its home plane. You must make a melee spell attack against the creature. On a hit, the creature must succeed on a Charisma saving throw or be sent back to its home plane in a random location.

At Higher Levels: If you cast this spell using an 8th-level spell slot or higher, you can affect two additional creatures for each level above 7th.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 40-foot line that is 5 feet wide and deals 11d6 force damage plus 1d6 force damage for each slot level above 7th.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 128 (Indie)

fields.name: Spiritual Vision (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a glass sphere the size of an eye)
fields.classes: School: Evocation, Touch Spells, Elementalist (Tanares), Elementalist (Tanares) (Spirit)
fields.text:
Element: Spirit

You touch a willing creature that gains truesight for the duration of the spell. In addition, it can see the ethereal plane and secret doors with a range of 120 feet.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 40-foot line that is 5 feet wide and deals 10d6 force damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 129 (Indie)

fields.name: Static Field (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Lightning

You create a 20-foot radius sphere centered on a point within range, charged with static electricity. Creatures that move within the area take 1d4 lightning damage for every 5 feet they move.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 30-foot line that is 5 feet wide and deals 2d6 lightning damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 129 (Indie)

fields.name: Steal Oxygen (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Air

You suppress the air from the lungs of a creature within range that you can see. The creature must make a Constitution saving throw, receiving 3 levels of exhaustion and becoming paralyzed on a failed save. For the duration, at the start of each of its turns, the creature must make a Constitution saving throw, suffering an additional 3 levels of exhaustion on a failed save or ending the effects on itself on a success. This spell has no effect on creatures that do not need to breathe, such as constructs or undead.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 45-foot cone and deals 14d6 thunder damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 129 (Indie)

fields.name: Stone Hand (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a small, flexible wire)
fields.classes: School: Evocation, Touch Spells, Elementalist (Tanares), Elementalist (Tanares) (Earth)
fields.text:
Element: Earth

You touch a creature, causing a collection of stones to gather and form an arm of stone that connects with the target's torso. The stone hand can hold and manipulate objects just like a regular hand, but it is not capable of attacking or performing somatic components for spells.
	The target gains the following benefits while the spell is in effect:

	• The target can wield a two-handed weapon or a versatile weapon with two hands, while still using the third hand to hold a shield or perform any other action that would normally require a free hand.

	• The target can use the third hand to hold a card or other small object in a way that is hidden from view, granting advantage on Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) checks made to cheat at games of chance.

	• The target can use the third hand to manipulate objects that would normally require the use of both hands, such as picking a lock or disarming a trap. If using three hands, the target gains advantage on any Dexterity checks made to interact with objects in this way.

	• The target can use the third hand to retrieve or stow an object that is normally out of reach, such as a potion on a high shelf or a weapon on the ground. The hand can reach up to 10 feet away from the target and can manipulate objects weighing up to 5 pounds. It must still use the appropriate action to do so.

	• The target can use the third hand to perform simple tasks, such as carrying a torch, holding a door open, or carrying a small object while using both of its regular hands for something else.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals 2d6 acid damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 129 (Indie)

fields.name: Stone Heart (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a gemstone worth at least 50 gp)
fields.classes: School: Evocation, Touch Spells, Elementalist (Tanares), Elementalist (Tanares) (Earth)
fields.text:
Element: Earth

You touch a creature and grant it protection against death effects for the duration of the spell. When casting the spell, you can use one to four gems, each worth at least 50 gp, which will fuse with the target. For each gem consumed at the time of casting, the target has one use of the following effects:

	• When reduced to 0 hit points, instead it remains at 1 hit point.

	• When subjected to an effect that would kill it instantly without dealing damage, the effect is negated.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals 7d6 acid damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 129 (Indie)

fields.name: Stone Imprisonment (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Earth

You create hands of stone on the ground to grasp any creatures of your choice inside a 10-foot-radius area within range. Each creature must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be restrained by one of the hands. A creature restrained remains in this condition until the spell ends or the hand grasping it is destroyed. Each hand has an AC of 16, 5 HP, is resistant to slashing and piercing damage, and immune to poison and psychic damage. If a hand reaches 0 hit points, it is destroyed.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals 2d6 acid damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 130 (Indie)

fields.name: Stone Shield (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Earth

When you are hit by an attack or forced to make a Dexterity saving throw, you can take a reaction to raise a shield of stone from the ground that protects you from attacks. Until the beginning of your next turn, you gain a +4 bonus to your AC and Dexterity saving throws, including against the triggering attack.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals acid damage, and on the damage roll treat every 1 or 2 as a 3.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 130 (Indie)

fields.name: Stone Sphere (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a glass sphere and a gravel of similar size)
fields.text:
Element: Earth

A sphere of stone envelops a creature or object of Large size or smaller within range of the spell. A non-voluntary creature must make a Dexterity saving throw, becoming trapped within the sphere on a failure.
	The stone sphere is magically reinforced, preventing any magical movement from inside to outside or vice versa. No sound passes through the stone, and those inside cannot see anything outside the sphere, including by magical means. They are under total cover and cannot be harmed by attacks and effects originating from outside.
	The sphere has an AC of 17 and 75 hit points, is immune to poison and psychic damage, and has resistance to any other type of damage except for damage from the disintegrate spell. It can support any amount of weight inside or on top of it and weighs around 1000 pounds, plus the weight of what is inside. Creatures capable of carrying or pushing the weight of the sphere can do so.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals 7d6 acid damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 130 (Indie)

fields.name: Subtle Influence (HB)
fields.text:
Type: Fire

You manipulate the mind of a creature within range, subtly influencing their emotions and behavior. Choose one of the following effects to apply to the target.

	• Aversion: The target develops a strong aversion to a creature or object of your choice, becoming slightly nauseous by its presence and avoiding it when possible.

	• Change Mood: You can influence the person's mood, causing them to feel overall happy, angry, sad, or agitated, affecting their behavior accordingly. This will not force a creature to attack or stop a combat, but will influence its overall mood.

	• Attraction: The target feels a strong attraction to a creature or object of your choice, seeking to approach and interact with it in a non-threatening manner. This effect does not end combat, but may make the target less likely to harm or kill the object of their attraction, not putting itself in danger while doing so.

	• Anger: The target feels anger toward a creature or object of your choice, seeking to harm it or break it. In combat, if an enemy is chosen, the target may make this enemy a preferred target. The creature will not attack or do anything that would be against its principles or would endanger itself The target must make a Wisdom saving throw to resist the spell's effect. If the target fails the saving throw, they are affected by the chosen effect for the spell's duration.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the spell's duration increases to 2 hours (3rd level), 4 hours (4th level), 8 hours (6th level), 24 hours (8th level), or 7 days (9th level).

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals 2d6 fire damage plus 1d6 fire damage for each slot level above 2nd.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 130 (Indie)

fields.name: Summon Flame Dragon (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a ruby worth at least 500 gp)
fields.text:
Element: Fire

You summon a dragon spirit that manifests in the form of a dragon. The spirit's physical form uses the stat block of a young brass dragon, but its only breath attack available is Fire Breath. It has its own turn and place in initiative, and will assist you to the best of its ability for the duration. When you cast this spell, choose between red, brass and gold, and the spirit will take on the appearance of that type of dragon. If the dragon is reduced to 0 hit points or you lose concentration, the spell ends and the dragon disappears.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 30-foot cone and deals 11d6 fire damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 131 (Indie)

fields.name: Summon Plant Servant (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a handful of leaves, mud and sticks)
fields.text:
Element: Plant

You conjure a plant servant. You choose an area rich in vegetation that fills a 10-foot cube within range. The vegetation joins together and forms a plant creature of CR 5 or lower in a space up to 10 feet from the point of origin. The plant obeys you to the best of its ability and acts after you in the initiative order. You can give simple action commands, such as attacking a target or running in a direction, as a free action. If you want to give a longer command, you must use a bonus action. If you lose concentration, the plant servant will continue to follow the last command until it completes it. If the plant servant completes its action and cannot hear or receive new commands, it will take the Dodge action and protect itself as best it can.
	You can use an action to regain concentration on this spell a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus. The plant disappears when it drops to 0 hit points or when the spell ends.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge infuse your plant servant with energy, allowing it to use an action to cast the elemental surge cantrip as if it were you, only once during the spell's duration, dealing 5d6 poison damage and requires a Constitution saving throw

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 131 (Indie)

fields.name: Sweet Dreams (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Water

You cause a creature within your line of sight to immediately fall asleep and have wonderful dreams. The creature can make a Wisdom saving throw to resist. If failed, it falls asleep. If the creature sleeps until the end of the spell's duration, the sleeping creature recovers as if it had taken a long rest. A creature affected by the effects of this spell can only be targeted again after completing a normal long rest. If cast before this condition is met, the spell has no effect. You can only benefit from another long rest after 24 hours.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge can create a thin layer of water around the creature, granting it 7d6 temporary hit points for 10 minutes.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 131 (Indie)

fields.name: Symbiosis (HB)
fields.classes: School: Transmutation, Touch Spells, Elementalist (Tanares), Elementalist (Tanares) (Plant)
fields.text:
Element: Plant

You touch a willing creature and create a symbiotic plant that intertwines with it. When the plant attaches to the target, it nullifies any poisoned condition it had before the spell.
	While attached to the plant, the target creature is immune to the poisoned condition and poison damage, and if it takes a short rest in a location illuminated by sunlight, all hit dice it spends during the rest heal the maximum value, and each die also adds the target's proficiency bonus to it. If the target takes any fire damage, the plant dies automatically.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals 5d6 poison damage and requires a Constitution saving throw.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 131 (Indie)

fields.name: Terracotta Army (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Earth

You conjure spirits of the earth that take the physical form of terracotta soldiers. You can conjure up to 16 soldiers and each one uses the stat block of an animated armor. You have a telepathic link and all soldiers listen to your orders mentally.
	They all act after you in the initiative order and will follow your orders as best as they can. You can give simple course of action commands, such as attacking a target or running in a direction, as a free action. If you want to give a command the size of a sentence, you must use an action. If you lose concentration, the soldiers will continue to follow the last command until it is completed. If the soldiers complete the designated action and cannot obtain new commands, they will use the Dodge action to preserve themselves as best as possible. At the end of the spell, all the spirits turn to dust.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals acid damage and affects a 45-foot cone. Each terracotta soldier inside the area won't take this damage, absorbing the acid instead. If a terracotta soldier is reduced to 0 hit points, it will explode in acid, forcing all creatures within 5 feet of it to make a Dexterity saving throw or take 2d6 acid damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 131 (Indie)

fields.name: Through the Water (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Water

You join your hands and focus, enveloping you and up to six willing creatures within 5 feet of you in a brilliant purple water. All the targets must be fully submerged in any liquid at the time of the casting, and they are teleported to another water source within 1 mile, through which you and the targets emerge. The destination is chosen by you and must be a known location.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 30-foot cone and deals 11d6 cold damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 132 (Indie)

fields.name: Thunderburst (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Air

You clap your hands, generating a 30-foot cone of thunderous shock. All creatures in the area must make a Constitution saving throw or become deafened. A creature deafened by this spell is also incapacitated. At the beginning of each turn, a deafened creature can make a Constitution saving throw to end the spell's effect on itself on a success. Undead, constructs, and creatures naturally deafened or already under the deafened condition are immune to its effects.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals 7d6 thunder damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 132 (Indie)

fields.name: Tidal Investigation (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Water

During the spell's duration, you can use a bonus action to analyze an area within 60 feet of you, detecting any blood drops, small objects, and weapons hidden within the area. Whenever you detect blood drops, make an Intelligence (Investigation) check to determine what you have uncovered. You learn the following information based on the results of your check:

	• 10 or more: You determine if any creature spilled blood and how many there are and their types.

	• 13 or more: You determine the severity of injuries, knowing if each creature is dead or alive.

	• 16 or more: You determine any weaknesses of the creature, if any.

In addition, for the duration of the spell, you gain advantage on your first attack each turn you make against a creature whose blood you analyzed for weaknesses, even if that creature has none.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals cold damage, and on the damage roll, consider any result of 1 or 2 as 3.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 132 (Indie)

fields.name: Tide of Bubbles (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Water

You unleash a burst of bubbles in a 30-foot wide, 80-foot long line, affecting all creatures within. Creatures in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw or be engulfed in a bubble. Once trapped, a creature is considered underwater, incapacitated, and vulnerable to lightning damage. Its speed is reduced to 0, except for swimming speed. At the start of each of its turns, the trapped creature can make a Strength or Dexterity saving throw (its choice). On a successful save, it is no longer incapacitated but remains trapped inside the bubble. A creature can escape the bubble by destroying it. Each bubble has an AC of 17 and 30 hit points, is immune to acid, bludgeoning, cold, fire, lightning, poison, and psychic damage, and has resistance to non-magical slashing and piercing damage.
	Creatures outside the bubble can attack it, but if the attacker is Huge or smaller and uses a melee attack, it must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the attacking creature becomes trapped in another bubble that emerges from the first.
	If you lose concentration, the spell ends and all bubbles are destroyed. Creatures with a swimming speed automatically escape the bubble.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 30-foot cone and deals 11d6 cold damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 132 (Indie)

fields.name: Torrential Rain (HB)
fields.classes: School: Evocation, Ritual Caster, Elementalist (Tanares), Elementalist (Tanares) (Water)
fields.text:
Element: Water

You are able to control the water element around you, harnessing the clouds to create a downpour in an area, affecting the entire spell area.
	During the casting and up to two hours after, the rain continues to lash the region, increasing about 5 cubic centimeters of water every 10 minutes of rain. The excessive amount of water will cause rivers to flood regions, entire lands to flood, and other effects from torrential rains.
	All creatures in the rain, except you, have their movement halved. Each turn a creature remains in the area, it must make a Strength (Athletics) check or become prone.
	All natural and magical fire sources up to 3rd level are extinguished and the area becomes lightly obscured for all creatures except you.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 30-foot cone and deals 11d6 cold damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 132 (Indie)

fields.name: Tracing Thunder (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Lightning

When you cast this spell, you channel electricity into your feet. Until the end of your turn, your speed is doubled and you can take the Dash action as a bonus action. When you move, you do not provoke opportunity attacks and leave a trail of electrical energy in the spaces you pass through until the end of your next turn. A creature that enters one of the spaces through which you left a trail of energy must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, the creature takes 3d6 lightning damage and is restrained until the end of its turn.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 30-foot line that is 5 feet wide and deals 7d6 lightning damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 133 (Indie)

fields.name: Tread Tremor (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Earth

You stomp the ground, creating a directed seismic wave in a cone, turning the entire affected area into difficult terrain. Each creature in the cone must make a Strength saving throw or be pushed 10 feet back, take 2d4 bludgeoning damage, and fall prone. Walls and structures in the area, depending on how well-built they are, may be weakened or destroyed at the GM's discretion.

Elemental Flux: With your next elemental surge, you stomp the ground. All creatures in a 10-foot radius circle centered on you must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw, taking 2d6 bludgeoning damage and being knocked prone on a failed save.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 133 (Indie)

fields.name: True Levitation (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Air

24 hours You concentrate all your control over the force of the element, causing the power of the wind to lift entire locations and relocate them to another place. The spell affects a circular area of land within range with a half mile radius and 100 feet in depth, lifting the block of land, including everything it carries above it.
	Once in motion, the block moves 30 feet per turn, uninterruptedly in the last commanded direction. With a bonus action, you can make the block start moving, change the direction of movement, or stop it.
	The block of land can only move through spaces it can fit into. If the block has its movement interrupted by an object or volume of land equal to or larger than it for more than 1 minute, the spell ends. Once the spell ends, the block descends slowly until it lands on the ground.
	Once during the spell's duration, you can grant control (concentration) to another creature that has spellcasting. You can create a block of land that levitates permanently by casting the spell on the same block for a year and, on the last day, defining a creature that will receive control over its movement without needing to concentrate or have spellcasting abilities. If the creature dies or is willing, you can change the control to another creature with a new casting of this spell.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 45-foot cone and deals 10d6 thunder damage. If cast against the levitated block of land, it takes no damage but is pushed 90 feet in a direction of your choice.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 133 (Indie)

fields.name: Tunneling Arms (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a few hairs from a mole)
fields.text:
Element: Earth

Your limbs morph into powerful claws. For the duration of the spell, you gain a burrowing speed equal to your walking speed. If you come across pure rock terrain, you can burrow at half your speed. When you burrow, you leave behind a tunnel that can only be passed through by creatures of your size or smaller.
	The claws can also be used to attack, you are considered proficient with them and they deal slashing damage equal to 1d8 plus your Strength or Dexterity modifier.

Elemental Flux: With your next elemental surge, you stomp the ground. All creatures in a 10-foot-radius circle centered on you must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw, taking 4d6 bludgeoning damage and being knocked prone on a failed save.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 134 (Indie)

fields.name: Unflinching Stream (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Water

You imbue a willing creature with the essence of water. For the duration, the target gains 2d6 temporary hit points and advantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws. If the target loses all these temporary hit points, they still retain the advantage on their saving throws for the duration.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals cold damage and affects a 20-foot line that is 5 feet wide.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 134 (Indie)

fields.name: Veil of Invisibility (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (an eyelash encased in gum arabic)
fields.classes: School: Evocation, Touch Spells, Elementalist (Tanares), Elementalist (Tanares) (Air)
fields.text:
Element: Air

You change the air properties around a creature you touch, making it invisible to one other creature within 60 feet. Anything the target is wearing or carrying is also invisible as long as it remains on their person. If the target attacks or casts a spell, the spell ends.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you can choose one additional target to be invisible to the same creature for each slot level above 2nd.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals thunder damage, affects a 20-foot line that is 5 feet wide, and deals an extra 1d6 thunder damage for every 2 spell levels used above 1st.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 134 (Indie)

fields.name: Visions from the Image (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Air

You create an illusion of an object or person, similar to the major image spell. Additionally, while within the spell's range, you can see and hear as if you also occupies the space of the created image.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals 7d6 thunder damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 134 (Indie)

fields.name: Volcano (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Lava

You create a volcano from a point on the ground within range. From the moment you cast the spell, a volcano begins to rise from the ground, growing in four distinct stages. Each round you maintain concentration on this spell, it produces additional effects of the next stage.

First stage: When you cast the spell, a 20-foot-radius sphere around the point you choose becomes extremely hot, and the ground becomes scorching hot. Creatures that enter or start their turn within the area must make a Constitution saving throw, taking 6d8 fire damage on a failure or half as much on a success.

Second stage: The ground within the area of the first stage rises, transforming the area into difficult terrain and beginning to release toxic gasses. All creatures within the area and a further 20-foot radius must make a Constitution saving throw or become poisoned due to the toxic gasses. Additionally, the effects of the first stage increase to a 40-foot radius.

Third stage: The raised area explodes in lava, and all creatures in the 20-foot-radius sphere must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, they take 8d8 bludgeoning damage and 3d8 fire damage, are thrown 20 feet in the opposite direction, and become coated in lava. A creature coated in lava takes 8d8 fire damage at the start of each of its turns for the next minute, or until it is doused with 3 gallons of water or uses an action to clean itself. In addition, the area affected by the second stage increases to a further 20-foot radius, and the area affected by the first stage increases to a total of a 60-foot radius.

Fourth stage: A 20-foot-radius pool of lava forms at the center of the volcano, rising to a height of 40 feet and beginning to launch magma spheres into the surrounding area. The magma spheres strike three locations of your choice within 100 feet of the center and affect a 10-foot-radius circle. Creatures in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw or take 10d8 fire damage and become coated in lava on a failed save, or half as much damage and no coating on a successful save. Buildings within the affected area are destroyed, with the extent of the damage determined by the GM.

If you lose concentration on the spell, the volcano retreats, returning one stage per round, and ending after it retreats from the first stage.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a sphere of a 30-foot radius centered on you. All creatures in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking 14d6 fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 134 (Indie)

fields.name: Waive Magic (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a cup of water)
fields.text:
Element: Water

You use water to neutralize spells. With an action, you can target a creature, an object, or a magical effect within range. Any spell of 3rd level or lower on the target ends. Each spell of 4th level or higher requires you to make a Wisdom ability check (DC 10 + spell level), ending the spell on a success.
	When you cast this spell as a reaction, you can interrupt the casting of a spell, but you must still make the Wisdom ability check regardless of the spell's level, with disadvantage.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a 4th-level spell slot or higher, you automatically end spells of up to the same level as the slot used. When cast as a reaction, you gain a +2 bonus to the Wisdom ability check for each slot level above 3rd.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals 5d6 cold damage plus 1d6 cold damage for each slot level above 3rd.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 135 (Indie)

fields.name: Wall of Lava (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a hand-sized flame and ruby powder worth at least 50 gp, which the spell consumes)
fields.text:
Element: Lava

You sprinkle ruby dust over the flames, causing a barrier of pure magma to rise from the ground. You can choose the shape of the barrier to be either a straight line with a length of 60 feet, a height of 15 feet, and a width of 5 feet, or a circle with a diameter of 20 feet, a height of 15 feet, and a width of 5 feet. The barrier blocks the line of sight.
	When the barrier appears, every creature within its area is pushed to one side of it, as chosen by you, and must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking 5d8 fire damage and being covered in lava on a failure, or taking half damage and not being covered in lava on a success.
	A creature that is covered in lava takes 2d8 fire damage at the end of each of its turns until it is either doused in at least 3 gallons of water or takes an action to clean itself.
	A creature can move through the barrier, but it is a painful and slow process. For every 1 foot moved, the creature must spend an additional 4 feet of movement. A creature that chooses to cross becomes covered in lava and must make a Constitution saving throw, taking 6d8 fire damage on a failure or half as much damage on a success.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals 10d6 fire damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 135 (Indie)

fields.name: Wall of Spirits (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a translucent crystal or gem)
fields.text:
Element: Spirit

You create a translucent barrier at a point within range, for the duration. The barrier floats in the air and does not require support, appearing in any position you choose, either horizontal, vertical, or angled. It has a thickness of 1 inch and you can make it semi-spherical or spherical with a radius of up to 15 feet, or flat, creating up to ten panels of 10-foot by 10-foot, which must be contiguous. If the barrier appears in a creature's space that cannot pass through it (see below),
the creature is pushed to one side of your choice.
	When creating the barrier, you can set one creature type or alignment (good, evil, chaotic, lawful) that cannot pass through the barrier. All other creatures or alignments can pass through it normally, but the chosen type cannot pass through the barrier in any way. Attacks and spells of the chosen creature type are neutralized by the barrier, which is indestructible for them, even affecting the Ethereal Plane.
	A creature that is not of the chosen type can choose not to pass through the barrier, so it can walk on the barrier as if it were solid ground, but once it does, it cannot go back on that decision.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 40-foot line that is 5 feet wide and deals 8d6 force damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 135 (Indie)

fields.name: Water Blessing (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Water

You aid a willing creature. Whenever the target makes an attack roll or a saving throw before the spell ends, the target can roll a d4 and add the number rolled to the attack roll or saving throw.  Additionally, once during the spell's duration, the target can choose to roll another d20 for an attack or saving throw and use the new result, ending the spell.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals 2d6 cold damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 135 (Indie)

fields.name: Water Body (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a cup of clean water)

fields.name: Water Essence (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Water 

You have the power to control water in all its forms within range, creating a variety of magical effects.

	• You can alter the color and scent of up to 1 cubic foot of water, making it seem clean or dirty.

	• You can instantly chill, heat, evaporate, or freeze any liquid with a volume of up to 1 cubic foot, as long as no creatures are inside it.

	• You can create an instant and harmless sensory effect, such as the sound of rushing water, crashing waves, falling rain, a light mist, or even dampening or drying a surface. The effect must fit within a cube with a side length of 1 foot.

	• You can drain moisture from a small object or plants, such as a flower or fruit, extracting clear, potable water.

You can dismiss these effects with an action.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 136 (Indie)

fields.name: Water Restoration (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Water

A creature absorbs the ambient water to restore itself. The creature regains 50 hit points at the moment of casting and an additional 50 hit points at the start of its turns until the spell ends. Additionally, if the target remains under the effect of the spell for an entire hour, the water can permanently regrow lost limbs and body parts, exactly as the original.
	If the target is in contact with a large body of water, such as lakes, rivers, and seas, the effects above are accelerated. If the target remains in contact since the end of its last turn, it regains all its hit points at the start of its next turn, and any lost limbs and other body parts are fully restored if the target remains in contact for at least 1 minute.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 45-foot cone and deals 12d6 cold damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 136 (Indie)

fields.name: Water Tentacle (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Water

Your arms are enveloped in water, forming semi-solid tentacles. While the spell remains in effect, you can freely control the tentacles, increasing your reach by 15 feet, including for touch spells, and you are able to manipulate and drag objects as if they were your own hands.
	The tentacles can be used to attack, requiring a melee spell attack to hit and dealing bludgeoning damage equal to 1d10 + your Wisdom modifier. Additionally, as a bonus action, you can grapple a creature hit, which will also be restrained until the grapple ends (the difficulty to escape equals your spell save DC). While holding a creature, you cannot use the tentacles to obtain the other benefits of this spell.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 10-foot radius circle centered on you and deals 2d6 cold damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 137 (Indie)

fields.name: Whiff (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Air

You blow air and create a whirlwind that travels in a 30-foot long, 5-foot wide, and 15-foot high line, stopping at walls or solid structures. All creatures in the area, Large or smaller, must make a Strength saving throw. On a failure, the creatures are pushed 20 feet in a direction of your choice. If their movement is obstructed by an obstacle, they suffer 1d6 bludgeoning damage for every 10 feet moved.
	The gust also disperses gas or vapor, extinguishes unprotected flames, and causes protected flames, such as lanterns, to dance wildly, with a 50 percent chance to be extinguished.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals thunder damage, and on the damage roll, consider every 1 or 2 as a 3.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 137 (Indie)

fields.name: Wind Cover (HB)
fields.classes: School: Evocation, Touch Spells, Elementalist (Tanares), Elementalist (Tanares) (Air)
fields.text:
Element: Air

A creature you touch becomes invisible until the start of the next turn. Anything the target is wearing or carrying is invisible as long as it is on the target's person and the target can act normally.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each slot level above 2nd.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge creates a burst, which affects a 10-foot radius circle centered on you and deals 2d6 thunder damage plus 1d6 thunder damage for each slot level above 2nd.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 137 (Indie)

fields.name: Winds of Time (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Air

You breathe the winds of time over a creature or object, altering the temporal flow by accelerating its natural processes.
	When you cast the spell, you can choose to accelerate the aging process of the targeted creature or object by a factor of twenty, causing it to experience twenty times the normal effects of the passage of time. For example, you could cause a plant to grow to maturity in a matter of hours, accelerate the onset of a poison to take effect within seconds instead of minutes, or end a magical effect with a minimum duration of one minute instantly. This spell can age a touched creature or object by 20 days in one. If the target is a creature, it can make a Constitution saving throw to avoid this spell's effect on a success.
	Note that the spell only affects natural and mystical processes related to time, and does not affect the actions or abilities of the target. The spell can be used to affect a wide range of effects related to time, but the GM should determine the limits of the spell's effects and the potential consequences of using it in creative ways.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge affects a 30-foot cone and deals 8d6 thunder damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 137 (Indie)

fields.name: Windstorm Point (HB)
fields.text:
Element: Air

You create a whirlwind at a location of your choice. The point remains stationary for the duration. Whenever a creature other than you comes within 5 feet of it, that creature must make a Strength saving throw or be flung away in the direction established by you when the spell was cast. The creature is thrown 40 feet high and 20 feet away in that direction.

Elemental Flux: Your next elemental surge deals 7d6 thunder damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 137 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Bioluminescent Secretion (HB)
fields.components: (1 Insanity Point, +1 point per 5 feet added to cone size)
fields.text:
As a bonus action, you can generate a glowing, bioluminescent substance. This secretion illuminates an area within 5 feet with dim light and leaves a luminous trail wherever you move. After 8 hours, the mutation ends, and the emission fades entirely.
	You can prematurely end this mutation to discharge a larger, slick amount of secretion over a 15-foot cone on the ground, rendering it as difficult terrain. All creatures within this area must pass a Dexterity saving throw or fall prone. A creature that either enters or ends its turn in this area must also make the Dexterity saving throw. The area stays illuminated and slippery for 8 hours.
	You can augment the size of the cone, up to a maximum of +25 feet, gaining 1 extra Insanity Point for every additional 5 feet. Your total Insanity Points cannot exceed the limit when enlarging the area. Also, you cannot use this power if you are at your Insanity Point maximum.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 150 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Dark Energy (HB)
fields.components: (1 Insanity Point, +1 per extra point of damage (see below))
fields.text:
Before rolling for an attack, you can, as a free action, infuse your weapons with dark energy. Until the start of your next turn, your next successful attack deals an additional 1d6 necrotic damage. Before the attack roll, you can choose to gain extra Insanity Points to bolster this damage, as long as the total points gained per use of this mutation do not exceed your madwalker level. For each extra Insanity Point you gain, add 1 to the necrotic damage roll. The total Insanity Points gained cannot exceed your current Insanity Point limit, except when using this mutation without gaining extra points.
	For instance, a 3rd-level madwalker using this power can gain 1 Insanity Point to deal an extra 1d6 necrotic damage, 2 points to deal 1d6+1, or 3 points to deal 1d6+2. However, she couldn't gain 4 points, as it would exceed her level. If the current Insanity Point total is 10 and the limit is 12, she can only gain 1 or 2 points on this power. Once she reaches 12 points, she can still use this power (+1d6) but can no longer increase its damage.

Note: This ability enables a madwalker to rapidly elevate her insanity level if she wishes to reach the Penumbral Shape sooner.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 150 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Elastic Limbs (HB)
fields.text:
With a bonus action, you can distort your limbs, elongating them. For the next 10 minutes, your melee attack reach increases by 5 feet, and your base walking speed increases by 10 feet. If you take bludgeoning damage, you may use your reaction to end this effect and reduce the damage by 2d8.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 150 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Horrid Tentacle (HB)
fields.text:
With a bonus action, you can conjure a grotesque tentacle from your back, extending up to 10 feet. This aberrant limb persists for 1 minute. The tentacle can execute only the following tasks:

	• As an action, you can pull, drag, or lift an object or willing creature, or cling onto something. When performing these actions, you can carry twice the weight your Strength normally allows.

	• As a bonus action, the tentacle can interact with objects. For instance, it can open or shut containers and doors, utilize keys, activate levers, push buttons, grasp small objects, and other similar tasks, subject to the GM's discretion.

	• The tentacle can function as an auxiliary limb, granting you advantage on Dexterity (Acrobatics) or Strength (Athletics) checks.

	• The tentacle can be used as a melee weapon endowed with light and finesse properties. It has a reach of 10 feet and deals 1d10 bludgeoning damage. If you're wielding a weapon in one hand, the tentacle can serve as a second light weapon for two-weapon combat.

	• The tentacle cannot wield a shield.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 150 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Penumbral Echoes (HB)
fields.text:
With a bonus action, you can manipulate your vocal cords for 1 minute, granting you the ability to emit sounds otherwise impossible to replicate. You can mimic any sound you've heard, be it from creatures (voices, grunts, growls) or objects (hammer clang, door creak, drops falling). A creature hearing the sound can attempt a DC 18 Wisdom (Insight) check to identify it as an imitation. With an action, you can end this mutation and release a frightful roar that resonates across a 10-foot radius. Each creature within range must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or suffer 2d4 thunder damage and be frightened for 1 minute. An affected creature must attempt a new Wisdom saving throw at the end of each of its turns. Upon success, the effect ceases and the creature becomes immune to it for the next 24 hours.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 150 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Penumbral Gaze (HB)
fields.text:
With a bonus action, you can channel penumbral energy through your eyes, causing them to appear large and ghostly white. For 1 hour, you have the advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on vision. Additionally, you gain darkvision with a range of 60 feet, or double the range if you already have darkvision.
	With an action, you can end these effects and direct a force blast toward a creature. Make a ranged attack roll against a target within 60 feet of you using your Dexterity modifier and proficiency bonus. On a hit, the target takes 3d6 force damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 150 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Space Distortion (HB)
fields.text:
With a bonus action, you can bend penumbral energy to conjure a small portal, enabling your hands to interact with distant locations. Until the end of your turn, you can manipulate objects or creatures up to 30 feet away and transport small items.
	While this mutation is active, you can make melee attacks against targets within 30 feet of you. These attacks ignore cover, and you add your Wisdom modifier to the attack rolls.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 151 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Noxious Attack (HB)
fields.classes: Madwalker: Aberrant Mutations, Madwalker (Aberrant Arachnid Trail): Aberrant Mutations
fields.text:
Madness Trail: Aberrant Arachnid Trail

With a bonus action, you sprout glands in your hands that generate a venom, coating your weapon for 1 minute. Each successful weapon attack deals an extra 2 poison damage and bestows a poison marker on the target (maximum of four markers). Creatures with at least one poison marker must make a Constitution saving throw at the beginning of their turns. On a successful save, they remove all poison markers. On a failure, they suffer 2 poison damage per poison marker.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 151 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Shadow Web (HB)
fields.classes: Madwalker: Aberrant Mutations, Madwalker (Aberrant Arachnid Trail): Aberrant Mutations
fields.text:
Madness Trail: Aberrant Arachnid Trail

With an action, you can create spiderwebs from your fingertips that last for 1 minute. The webs can stretch up to 60 feet, with varying effects:

	• You can launch a web at an object and pull it towards you. If it is heavier than 10 pounds, you must pull it using your own Strength.

	• You can affix the web to objects or solid surfaces, granting advantage on Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks when climbing.

	• You can use the web to obstruct an area up to 20 feet in diameter between two solid objects; a creature entering the blocked area must succeed on a Strength ability check or become restrained until the end of its next turn.

	• You can aim a web at a creature within range. If the creature fails a Dexterity saving throw, it is restrained for the duration of the effect. It can attempt a Strength saving throw at the end of each of its turns to end the condition.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 151 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Mind Slash (HB)
fields.classes: Madwalker: Aberrant Mutations, Madwalker (Nightmare's Augury Trail): Aberrant Mutations
fields.text:
Madness Trail: Nightmare's Augury Trail

With your action, you unleash a surge of psychic power against a creature you can see within 60 feet of you, dealing 3d8 psychic damage. The target makes an Intelligence saving throw to reduce the damage by half. On a fail, the target also has disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes until the end of your next turn.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 152 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Psychic Bond (HB)
fields.classes: Madwalker: Aberrant Mutations, Madwalker (Nightmare's Augury Trail): Aberrant Mutations
fields.text:
Madness Trail: Nightmare's Augury Trail

As a bonus action, you can establish a telepathic bond with an ally within 120 feet of you. The link lasts for 1 hour or until the creature moves beyond range. This bond allows you to communicate with the chosen creature as though engaged in normal conversation. Furthermore, for the duration of the link, both can use the Help action on Intelligence ability checks made even at a distance.
	Alternatively, this mutation can be used against a hostile creature to access its surface thoughts. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw; otherwise, you discern its emotional state, and it has disadvantage on all attacks against you until your the start of next turn.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 152 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Amphibious Skin (HB)
fields.text:
With an action, you can modify your skin to make it slippery, changing your base AC to 13 + your Dexterity modifier. This grants you advantage on ability checks and saving throws to escape the grappled condition.
	Additionally, you grow gills on your neck that allow you to breathe underwater, and your limbs are adapted to provide a swimming speed equal to your base walking speed. These effects last for 8 hours.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 152 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Body Shaping (HB)
fields.text:
With an action, you can alter your physical appearance for the next 8 hours. You can assume the form of any humanoid creature within your size category. Other attributes, such as your voice, scent, and mannerisms, remain the same. A creature must succeed on a DC 18 Intelligence (Investigation)
check to discern that your appearance is a disguise.
	If you assume the form of a creature that has charmed or frightened another one, the affected creature is also considered charmed or frightened by you while you maintain this form or until it sees through your disguise.
	Alternatively, you may use this mutation to enhance your body, granting you 2d6 temporary hit points for 1 minute.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 152 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Penumbral Leap (HB)
fields.text:
As a bonus action, you can disappear into the Penumbral Plane and move instantly, reappearing in a space you can see up to 30 feet away.
	Alternatively, you can use the Penumbral Leap to get a brief glimpse of the Penumbra from your current position in the Material Plane. Make a Wisdom (Perception) check to gather information about the penumbral environment, creatures, and any other pertinent details you can glean at a quick glance, based on the DC set by the GM.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 153 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Shadow Clones (HB)
fields.text:
As an action, you can create two illusionary copies of yourself made of penumbral energy. They occupy the same space as you and move with you for 1 minute, mirroring your every action and randomly shifting positions around your body, making them indistinguishable from you. For the duration of this mutation, each time a creature targets you with an attack, roll a d20 to determine whether the attack instead targets one of your clones. With two clones, you must roll an 8 or higher. With one clone, you must roll an 11 or higher.
	A clone's AC equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier. If an attack hits a clone, it is destroyed.
	If a creature adjacent to you is attacked, you can take a reaction to confuse the attacker with one of your clones and impose disadvantage on the attack roll, destroying the clone.
	These are the only ways to destroy a clone, as it ignores all damage and effects.
	Creatures that don't rely on sight or can see through illusions (such as truesight) are unaffected by this mutation.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 153 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Warped Physique (HB)
fields.text:
With a bonus action, for the next 1 minute, you can distort and enhance your muscles and tendons, giving your legs exceptional strength and flexibility. Your long jump covers a distance equal to your walking speed, and your high jump covers a distance equal to half your walking speed. While this mutation is active, you have advantage on Dexterity (Acrobatics) and Strength (Athletics) checks involving jumps.
	Alternatively, before making a melee weapon attack, you can use all your leg strength to end this Mutation and augment the damage. On a hit, your attack deals an extra 2d8 damage of the same type of the weapon.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 153 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Pain Toxin (HB)
fields.classes: Madwalker: Aberrant Mutations, Madwalker (Aberrant Arachnid Trail): Aberrant Mutations
fields.text:
Madness Trail: Aberrant Arachnid Trail

As an action, you emit a toxic blast in a 20-foot cone. Every creature within this cone must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, the creature is afflicted by the poison. At the start of each of its turns, an affected creature must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or spend its action writhing in pain. The effect ends when an affected creature succeeds on three (nonconsecutive) Constitution saving throws or uses an action to cleanse itself with fresh water. Creatures immune to poison are unaffected by this mutation. After succeeding on three Constitution saving throws, the creature becomes immune to the effect for 24 hours.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 153 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Venom Splash (HB)
fields.classes: Madwalker: Aberrant Mutations, Madwalker (Aberrant Arachnid Trail): Aberrant Mutations
fields.text:
Madness Trail: Aberrant Arachnid Trail

As an action, you unleash a blast of venom in a 20-foot cone. Any creature within the cone must make a Constitution saving throw, suffering 3d10 poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 153 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Mind Drain (HB)
