fields.classes: Madwalker: Aberrant Mutations, Madwalker (Nightmare's Augury Trail): Aberrant Mutations
fields.text:
Madness Trail: Nightmare's Augury Trail

As an action, you try to touch a creature, making a melee attack roll. On a hit, you deal 5d8 psychic damage and regain hit points equal to half the damage dealt. If your target is grappled, your touch attack automatically hits.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 153 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Psychic Weapon (HB)
fields.classes: Madwalker: Aberrant Mutations, Madwalker (Nightmare's Augury Trail): Aberrant Mutations
fields.text:
Madness Trail: Nightmare's Augury Trail

When you hit a target with a melee attack, you can activate this mutation to deal an extra 2d6 psychic damage to it. Additionally, until the end of your next turn, the affected creature has disadvantage on any saving throw against the charmed or frightened conditions.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 153 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Aberrant Gaze (HB)
fields.text:
As a bonus action, multiple eyes sprout all over your body, enhancing your vision for 1 minute. During this time, you see in all directions, cannot be surprised, gain advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks related to sight, and receive a +2 bonus to your AC. Additionally, you can use an action to focus your eyes on a creature within 30 feet of you. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be restrained for 1 minute. An affected creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of its turns, ending the effect on a success. Using this action ends the mutation.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 153 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Aberrant Spines (HB)
fields.text:
As a bonus action, you manipulate your bone structure to sprout spikes from your skin. For 1 minute, these spines can be used as light weapons, with the finesse and thrown properties (range 20/60), dealing 1d10 piercing damage. Upon hitting a creature, it must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or its speed is halved. At the start of each turn, the creature can attempt another saving throw to negate this effect for that turn.
	If the creature is near a wall or large object when hit, it becomes pinned to that surface, receiving the restrained condition. It can make a Strength saving throw at the start of each turn to free itself. Removing a spine requires an action and inflicts 1d8 slashing damage, but a DC 18 Wisdom (Medicine) check can avoid this damage.
	Additionally, you can launch spines into a wall or steep surface to form handholds, granting advantage on Strength (Athletics) checks for climbing. After a minute, the effect ends, and any remaining spines disintegrate.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 153 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Interplanar Vortex (HB)
fields.text:
As an action, you form a void portal under a creature within 60 feet of you. The creature must make a Dexterity saving throw. If it fails, it plummets into the portal and suffers 6d10 necrotic damage from the penumbral energies within before being ejected against the ground by another portal that appears 30 feet above a chosen point on the ground within range, taking falling damage and landing prone. Any other creature at the landing point must also make a Dexterity saving throw or suffer the same falling damage and prone condition. If successful, it avoids the damage and becomes prone. Alternatively, you can control the harmful energies to allow an ally to pass through the portal to another one you create within 60 feet. In this case, the ally must succeed on a Constitution saving throw to avoid the necrotic damage, halving it on a failed save.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 154 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Shadow Control (HB)
fields.text:
With a bonus action, you can use your shadow to attempt to paralyze a creature up to 30 feet away. The creature must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or be paralyzed for 1 minute. To maintain this effect, you must forfeit your actions, reactions, and movement, and can only use bonus actions. You cannot take damage, or the effect ends immediately. At the start of each turn, the paralyzed creature can make a Wisdom saving throw to end the effect. During this time, you can use your bonus action to create a shadowy tentacle that extends up to 5 feet from the paralyzed creature and attacks. The tentacle deals 2d6 necrotic damage on a hit, reducing the creature's maximum hit points until it finishes a long rest.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 154 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Volatile Mutation (HB)
fields.text:
As a bonus action, you can alter your body, causing your muscles to swell and acid-filled pustules to form on your skin. For 1 minute, every attack you suffer triggers a 10-foot cone of acid in the direction of the attack. Each creature within this cone takes 1d6 acid damage. Additionally, during this period, you gain resistance to acid damage and have advantage on Charisma (Intimidation) checks.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 154 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Arachnid Legs (HB)
fields.classes: Madwalker: Aberrant Mutations, Madwalker (Aberrant Arachnid Trail): Aberrant Mutations
fields.text:
Madness Trail: Aberrant Arachnid Trail

You sprout four spider-like legs from your back that last for 1 minute, enhancing your speed by 10 feet. Their sharp and durable nature allows you to use them as weapons that deal 1d8 slashing damage. On a hit, the target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, the target takes an extra 1d8 poison damage and becomes poisoned. In addition, you can use your bonus action to make an extra attack with one of the spider legs.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 154 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Venomous Saliva (HB)
fields.classes: Madwalker: Aberrant Mutations, Madwalker (Aberrant Arachnid Trail): Aberrant Mutations
fields.text:
Madness Trail: Aberrant Arachnid Trail

As a bonus action, you can spit venom at a creature within 15 feet of you. The creature must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or take 3d12 poison damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 155 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Telepathic Mindlink (HB)
fields.classes: Madwalker: Aberrant Mutations, Madwalker (Nightmare's Augury Trail): Aberrant Mutations
fields.text:
Madness Trail: Nightmare's Augury Trail

With a bonus action, you establish a mental link between yourself and a willing creature. The connection lasts for 1 hour or until you choose to end it or fall unconscious. During this time, you can telepathically communicate with the creature within your line of sight over any distance or up to 40 feet away when out of sight. If the creature is familiar to you, the communication range increases to 120 feet when out of sight. This ability is affected by effects that prevent magic or magical communication. You can maintain a bond with up to 3 creatures simultaneously; establishing a new link with a fourth creature breaks the connection with the first.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 155 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Waves of Headache (HB)
fields.classes: Madwalker: Aberrant Mutations, Madwalker (Nightmare's Augury Trail): Aberrant Mutations
fields.text:
Madness Trail: Nightmare's Augury Trail

Using your action, you emit mental pulses that affect all creatures within 15 feet of you. Each affected creature must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, it suffers severe headaches, taking 6d6 psychic damage and falling prone from the pain. On a successful save, it takes half damage and remains upright.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 156 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Assassin's Stain (HB)
fields.text:
Using your bonus action, you can mark an enemy up to 30 feet away with penumbral energy, causing an extra 1d8 necrotic damage each time you hit this enemy with an attack over the next minute. Only one enemy can bear this mark at a time.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 156 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Bat Parts (HB)
fields.text:
As an action, you can take on the qualities of a penumbral bat, gaining a set of distortive wings that provide a flying speed of 30 feet, blindsight within a 60-foot radius, and clawed feet capable of grabbing objects and creatures up to one size larger than yours.
	While flying, you can use your bonus action to make a proficient melee weapon attack to grab a target on a hit, enabling you to carry items or creatures weighing up to 45 times your Strength score without penalties to your speed, or weighing above that to a maximum of 90 times your Strength score, but your speed is halved.
	This transformation lasts 10 minutes, and you can opt to extend its duration for an additional 10 minutes by gaining 3 more Insanity Points. If you're in the air when the effect ends and you don't extend it, you fall immediately.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 156 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Charge of Shadows (HB)
fields.text:
With a bonus action, you charge your held weapons with penumbral energy. For the following minute, your next successful attack deals an extra 2d8 necrotic damage. Additionally, the target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or become incapacitated for 1 minute, being able to make a new saving throw at the end of each of its turns to end this condition.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 156 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Penumbral Eruption (HB)
fields.text:
As an action, you manipulate penumbral energies to create two portals up to 30 feet apart. An eruption of penumbral energy streaks between these portals, forcing any creature within a 10-foot wide line extending the distance between the portals to make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, they suffer 4d8 necrotic damage and 4d8 force damage, taking half as much damage on a successful save. The portals vanish at the end of the turn.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 156 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Penumbral Fog (HB)
fields.text:
With an action, you can amplify the effects of the Penumbral Plane on the material world, creating a 20-foot radius sphere of fog centered on a point up to 60 feet away from you. All creatures within this zone, except you, must make a Constitution saving throw or suffer 3d6 psychic damage. The area remains heavily obscured to all creatures except you for 10 minutes.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 156 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Allergenic Spores (HB)
fields.classes: Madwalker: Aberrant Mutations, Madwalker (Aberrant Arachnid Trail): Aberrant Mutations
fields.text:
Madness Trail: Aberrant Arachnid Trail

As a bonus action, you emit a cloud of toxic spores, extending up to 10 feet in all directions. Any creature within the area must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or suffer 2d6 poison damage and become poisoned, taking half damage and avoiding the poisoned condition on a successful save.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 156 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Pheromone Spray (HB)
fields.classes: Madwalker: Aberrant Mutations, Madwalker (Aberrant Arachnid Trail): Aberrant Mutations
fields.text:
Madness Trail: Aberrant Arachnid Trail

As an action, you alter your glands to produce potent pheromones that radiate up to 60 feet around you for the next hour. Any humanoid creature that enters or starts its turn in this area must make a Constitution saving throw. Creatures engaged in combat with you have advantage on this saving throw.
	Those who fail are charmed by you, viewing you as a friendly acquaintance, while those who succeed are unaffected. Creatures immune to poison or those that don't need to breathe automatically succeed. Winds of moderate or greater speed disperse your pheromones, negating this effect.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 156 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Minor Telekinesis (HB)
fields.classes: Madwalker: Aberrant Mutations, Madwalker (Nightmare’s Augury Trail): Aberrant Mutations
fields.text:
Madness Trail: Nightmare's Augury Trail

As a bonus action, you can manipulate objects up to 30 feet away from you, provided their total weight doesn't exceed 30 times your Wisdom score. If an object isn't worn or carried, you can move it up to 30 feet in any direction. Worn or carried items require the owner to fail a Strength saving throw for you to move them. Your telekinetic control also allows you to handle small objects delicately, open containers, retrieve or store items, or pour out the contents of a vial. This control lasts up to 10 minutes.
	Alternatively, as an action, you can use your telekinesis to hurl a creature up to one size larger than you up to 30 feet away in any direction of your choosing. If this creature collides with a solid structure or another creature, it suffers 6d10 bludgeoning damage and falls prone. The creature it collides with can make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage and to avoid falling prone.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 156 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Penumbral Attraction (HB)
fields.classes: Madwalker: Aberrant Mutations, Madwalker (Nightmare’s Augury Trail): Aberrant Mutations
fields.text:
Madness Trail: Nightmare's Augury Trail

With an action, you can hypnotize a humanoid creature within 60 feet of you, subjecting them to the effects of the dominate person spell for the next minute.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 157 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Deadly Tentacles (HB)
fields.text:
As a bonus action, you can sprout four tentacles from your back that last for 1 minute or until you retract them with another bonus action. You can use your action to attack with them, making four attacks, one with each tentacle. They have a 10-foot reach, use either your Strength or Dexterity for the attack and damage rolls, and deal 3d4 bludgeoning damage per hit.
	When a creature enters a space within reach of a tentacle, you can lash out with an immediate attack (as a free action) up to four times until the start of your next turn. Successful hits can be used to grapple the target, automatically dealing damage at the start of each of its turns. As an action, a grappled creature can attempt to escape with a successful Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check against a DC 20. A grappling tentacle cannot attack.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 157 (Indie)

name: Aberrant Mutation: In a Blink of an Eye (HB)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: In a Blink of an Eye (HB)
fields.text:
With a bonus action, you can forsake your movement to teleport adjacent to a visible enemy within 40 feet of you. Your attacks against this enemy have advantage until the end of your turn. When your turn ends, you can immediately teleport yourself to any other space within 40 feet of your current position.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 157 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Nefarious Dinner (HB)
fields.text:
You contort your facial muscles grotesquely, your jaw reconfiguring into a fanged maw capable of tearing a creature apart. Upon invoking this mutation, make a proficient melee weapon attack against a creature. On a hit, you bite the creature, dealing 7d8 slashing damage and 7d8 necrotic damage, and causing a bleeding effect.
	The bleeding creature takes 1d10 necrotic damage at the start of each of its turns and can attempt a Constitution saving throw at the end of each of its turns to staunch the bleeding. If your bite damage reduces a Medium or smaller creature to 0 hit points, you can consume it with a bonus action, earning temporary hit points equal to half the bite damage. These temporary hit points last for 1 hour.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 157 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Nightmare Whirlpool (HB)
fields.text:
By activating this power, you invade the minds of all creatures within 15 feet of you, creating a mental link with them that persists for 1 minute. Each targeted creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw, or suffer 6d8 psychic damage and perceive you and your allies as incarnations of their deepest fears due to memories you implant. They remain frightened of you and your allies for the duration.
	Alternatively, you can forgo the damage to implant different types of memories in those who fail their saving throw. Consult with your GM for potential uses. Affected creatures can attempt a new saving throw at the end of each of their turns, ending the effect on a success.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 158 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Parasitism (HB)
fields.text:
With a bonus action, you attempt to attach yourself onto a nearby creature, forcing it to make a Constitution saving throw. If it fails, you transform and graft yourself onto them, draining their vitality. The afflicted creature suffers 10d10 necrotic damage at the start of each of its turns, and you recover hit points equal to half the inflicted damage. The target's speed is reduced by 10 feet, and it can use an action to try to pry you off, making a Strength saving throw. On a success, you are dislodged and fall prone in an adjacent space. While leeching, you are unable to take actions, bonus actions, or reactions, and you are immobile, sticking to your host. Should the creature's hit points reach zero, your parasitic grip ceases, and you appear in an unoccupied adjacent space. At the start of your turn, while leeching, you can gain an extra Insanity Point to voluntarily detach and stand in a nearby unoccupied space.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 158 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Penumbra Blade (HB)
fields.text:
While making an attack, you can invoke this mutation to infuse your weapon with potent necrotic energy drawn from the Penumbral Plane. All attacks you make until the end of your turn deal an extra 4d6 necrotic damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 158 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Exoskeleton (HB)
fields.classes: Madwalker: Aberrant Mutations, Madwalker (Aberrant Arachnid Trail): Aberrant Mutations
fields.text:
Madness Trail: Aberrant Arachnid Trail

You use your action to create a penumbral energy exoskeleton that covers your body. For the next 10 minutes, all incoming damage (except psychic) is dealt to the exoskeleton's hit points first. It has 80 hit points and shares your damage resistances and immunities.
	If an attack dismantle your exoskeleton and its damage surpasses its residual hit points, the remaining damage is transferred to you.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 158 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Web Cocoon (HB)
fields.classes: Madwalker: Aberrant Mutations, Madwalker (Aberrant Arachnid Trail): Aberrant Mutations
fields.text:
Madness Trail: Aberrant Arachnid Trail

As an action, you adapt your body to emit a flood of webs at a creature up to one size larger than you within 20 feet of you. The creature must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or become restrained in the web cocoon, taking 3d8 bludgeoning damage at the end of each of its turns. The creature can be attacked as usual, with no effects on the cocoon.
	It remains trapped for up to 1 minute or until the cocoon is destroyed, which has an AC of 15, 30 hit points, and has vulnerability to fire damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 159 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Eye of Augury (HB)
fields.classes: Madwalker: Aberrant Mutations, Madwalker (Nightmare's Augury Trail): Aberrant Mutations
fields.text:
Madness Trail: Nightmare's Augury Trail

As an action, you close your eyes, which merge into a singular, large eye in the center of your face. For 1 minute, you gain truesight and can use your bonus action to take the Dodge or Disengage action. During this time, you can use an action to focus your eye on a creature within 40 feet of you, imposing a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, they suffer the effects of the confusion spell. Using this ability ends the mutation.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 159 (Indie)

fields.name: Aberrant Mutation: Phantom of Penumbra (HB)
fields.classes: Madwalker: Aberrant Mutations, Madwalker (Nightmare's Augury Trail): Aberrant Mutations
fields.text:
Madness Trail: Nightmare's Augury Trail

As an action, you create a penumbral projection of yourself and launch it at a target within 30 feet of you. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or take 4d6 psychic damage and become stunned for 1 minute. The projection then moves to another creature within 20 feet of you and imposes the same conditions, repeating up to 4 times. If a creature succeeds on the saving throw, the effect ends.
	A creature affected by this ability can make the saving throw again at the end of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 159 (Indie)

fields.name: Ammunition Eyes (HB)
fields.text:
When you cast this spell, you can make 1 to 20 arrows magically enchanted for the duration, making a special magical bond with each of them. You make any ranged attack using these arrows with advantage, as well as ignoring half cover and ¾ cover that protects the target of this attack. Also, for the duration of the spell, you always know where your enchanted arrows are, as well as you can use your action to magically see through one of those arrows of your choice, and continue to do so until you use your action to return to your normal senses. As long as you are seeing through the arrow, you are blind to your own senses. You will not be able to see through one of its arrows if it is more than 1 mile away from you. If one of these arrows breaks, the enchantment no longer affects it.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 280 (Indie)

fields.name: Amplify the Pain (HB)
fields.classes: School: Necromancy, Cleric, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard
fields.text:
You concentrate and gaze upon a creature within range, causing all of the pain it receives to be amplified for the duration of the spell. Whenever the target takes damage, it must make a Constitution saving throw or take an additional 1d8 necrotic damage. If this additional damage reduces the target's hit points to 10 or fewer, it must make a Strength saving throw or drop anything it is holding on a failed save.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 280 (Indie)

fields.name: Arena's Fervor (HB)
fields.text:
When you cast this spell, you instill in you and your allies the spirit of the arena. You and every willing ally within 20 feet of you has advantage on Strength ability checks, Strength saving throws and all saving throws against effects that cause the frightened condition. While a creature has this effect active, it deals +2 on all damage rolls it makes, including attacks and spells. The bonus is applied to each damage caused individually before any other modifier.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 280 (Indie)

fields.name: Aurora Heal (HB)
fields.text:
When you cast this spell,.you create a 20-foot radius aura around you. Allied creatures that start their turns within the area regain hit points equal to 1d6 + your proficiency bonus. Also, it suppresses all magical effects that are causing a condition affecting allied creatures within the area. Lasting effects or conditions do not cease to affect the creature, but are only suspended for the duration of the spell.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 280 (Indie)

fields.name: Avelum's Force Spheres (HB)
fields.text:
You conjure five small energy spheres in range, each about 2 feet in diameter, spinning at high speed and affecting a spherical area with a diameter of 10 feet. Any creature that starts its turn or enters the area takes 3d6 force damage, or half damage with a successful Dexterity saving throw. As a bonus action, you can move each sphere up to 20 feet in any direction within the spell's range.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 280 (Indie)

fields.name: Banner of Inspiration (HB)
fields.text:
You create a fixed, 10 feet high, spiritual banner in a place within range, with a symbol you are currently defendeing.
	Allies within a 60-foot radius area around the banner and who can see it are inspired, and for the next 10 minutes, can add 1d6 to one ability check, attack roll, or saving throw.
	Each ally can only use this extra die once, ending this effect for them after it is used. For all purposes, this die counts as a Bardic Inspiration die. This spell can only be cast once

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 280 (Indie)

fields.name: Beacon of Envy (HB)
fields.classes: School: Abjuration, Bard, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard
fields.text:
You become a catalyst of envy, pulling the luck of an enemy towards you. When an enemy you can see makes a roll, such as an attack or a saving throw, the target must succeed on a Charisma check. If it fails, you steal that result and store it. If you do so, the target must reroll the dice that was stolen.
	While maintaining concentration, you can spend the stolen value as one of your own rolls, thus ending the effect of the spell.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 280 (Indie)

fields.name: Bite of the Naga Queen (HB)
fields.text:
You transform one of your arms into a serpent for a moment, allowing you to make a melee spell attack against a creature within 10 feet of you. On a hit, the target takes piercing damage equal to 1d8 + your spellcasting ability modifier and must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, the creature takes 10d8 poison damage and becomes poisoned. On a success, the creature takes half of the poison damage and is not poisoned.
	Alternatively, the serpent arm can spit the poison in a 10-foot cone, starting up to 10 feet from you, and all creatures in the area must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, they take 6d8 poison damage and become poisoned, taking 1d6 poison damage at the start of their turns. They can repeat the saving throw at the end of each turn, ending the condition on a success. Creatures poisoned by this spell cannot become poisoned by it again until they finish a long rest.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 281 (Indie)

fields.name: Black Dragon's Mantle (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (small portion of any dragon's material)
fields.text:
You infuse the body of a willing creature you touch with black flames that cover its entire body. The target becomes resistant to fire and necrotic damage. Any other creature that touches the target takes 1d6 fire damage + 1d6 necrotic damage. If the target takes damage from melee attacks, the attacking creature must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw for each attack or take damage as if it had touched the target. In addition, the same damage is caused to a creature if the target hits it with melee attacks or manage to touch it in any other way.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 281 (Indie)

fields.name: Blinding Armor (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (medium armor or higher)
fields.text:
Your armor emits a strong pulse of intense light capable of blinding opponents. Any hostile creature within 15 feet of you that can see you must make a Constitution saving throw and becomes blinded for 1 minute on a failure. Blinded creatures can roll a saving throw at the end of each of their turns to regain their sight.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 281 (Indie)

fields.name: Carry the Flame (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a sacred symbol the other person could carry)
fields.text:
Choose a spell you are able to cast that is of 4th level or lower. For the duration, you grant a creature within range the ability to cast that spell one time. The target creature uses its Wisdom as its spellcasting ability for that spell and must expend the actions and components as described for the spell.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 281 (Indie)

fields.name: Chorus of the Furious Animal (HB)
fields.text:
You emit a swift melody with a frenzied rhythm, provoking a beast creature to unleash its fury upon its foes. For the duration, the beast can make one more attack with one of its natural weapons, and has resistance to slashing, piercing, and bludgeoning damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 281 (Indie)

fields.name: Circle of Crystals (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a small citrine fruit worth at least 100 gp)
fields.text:
You and two other willing creatures of your choice that you can see within range gain resistance against two types of damage chosen from acid, bludgeoning, cold, fire, lightning, necrotic, piercing, poison. slashing, and thunder. If an affected creature already has resistance to a chosen damage type, it gain immunity to that damage for the spell's duration.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 7th level or higher, you can affect one more creature for each slot level above 6th.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 281 (Indie)

fields.name: Conjure Aberration (HB)
fields.text:
You call an aberrant creature of the penumbral plane to serve you. An aberration of challenge rating 5 or lower appears in an unoccupied space within range, creating a short distortion when it appears.
	The aberration is friendly to you and your companions for the duration. Roll initiative for the aberration, which has its own turns. It obeys any verbal commands that you issue to it (no action required by you). If you don't issue any commands to the aberration, it defends itself from hostile creatures but otherwise takes no actions.
	If your concentration is broken, the aberration doesn't disappear. Instead, you lose control of the aberration, it becomes hostile toward you and your companions, and it might attack. An uncontrolled aberration can't be dismissed by you, and it disappears 1 hour after you summoned it.
	The GM has the aberration's statistics.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 281 (Indie)

fields.name: Corrosive Tears (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a small acid flask)
fields.text:
You conjure a green cloud that drops a corrosive acid rain, affecting a 30-foot radius, 30-foot high cylinder centered on a point within range. When a creature enters the spell's area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, it must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, the creature takes 2d8 acid damage, or half as much damage on a success. Objects not being carried and structures in the affected area, take double damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 282 (Indie)

fields.name: Cupid's Arrow (HB)
fields.text:
You shoot a spectral arrow establishing a connection between two humanoid creatures within range (you can target yourself). Unwilling creatures must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be affected by the arrow.
	You make one or both of the affected creatures become charmed by the other (even if the other creature succeeded on the save). This can cause two creatures to become charmed by each other, or one creature to be charmed by the other, at your choice.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher you can charm any creature, not only humanoids.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 282 (Indie)

fields.name: Demigod Wings (HB)
fields.text:
You create six wings composed of condensed divine energy that sprout from your back. The wings grant you a flying speed of 50 feet for the duration of the spell. These wings have great powers and you can perform the following effects:

Wings of Mercy: As an action, you create an enormous gust of healing energy. All creatures in a 30-foot cone regains 5d10 hit points.

Wings of Vengeance: As an action, the wings emit a strong pulse of energy that affects a 30-foot-radius sphere around you, and hostile creatures in the area take 5d10 radiant damage.

Wings of Mercy: As a reaction, you can make the wings defend your body by folding around it. If you react to an attack, gain +10 to your AC until the start of your next turn. If you react to a spell, you gain advantage on the saving throw, or the bonus to your AC, if the spell requires an attack roll.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 282 (Indie)

fields.name: Echoing (HB)
fields.text:
You manipulate reality to create an echoing effect. As a reaction to the end of another creature's turn, you can cast this spell to replicate the effects of that turn. To use this spell, you must have witnessed the events of that turn within your line of sight. The replicated effects include spellcasting, attacks, damage, and the results of saving throws and ability checks. All targets remain the same, and any attacks or effects that become impossible, such as a target moving out of reach, will simply not occur. No additional dice rolls or checks are required, and the results of the replicated actions remain unchanged.
	It is important to note that casting echoing does not incur any additional costs or expenses, such as consuming spell slots or expending resources from abilities or spells. However, if the original action had any side effects on the caster, such as those caused by a wish spell, you will experience these side effects instead of the original creature, as if you had performed those actions yourself.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 282 (Indie)

fields.name: Edge of Mirrors (HB)
fields.text:
You create a number of small magic mirrors, equal to your spellcasting ability modifier, about half a foot square each, distributing them anywhere within the spell's range. The mirrors are invisible, but can be seen through spells such as detect magic, or by creatures that have true sight, or the like. You, and any creature you allow, are able to see the mirrors. When a creature that can see the mirrors is adjacent to one of them, it will be able to see what is reflected on all other mirrors.
	In addition, spellcasters who can see the mirrors, and are adjacent to any of them, can cast their spells as if they were positioned at the location of one of the other mirrors. The spell cast in this way cannot have the range of touch.
	Creatures that are in spaces adjacent to the space occupied by one of the mirrors can sense their presence with a successful DC 18 Wisdom (Perception) check. The mirrors have 5 hp, AC 13.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 282 (Indie)

fields.name: Electric Burning (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a bit of fur or wool)
fields.text:
You create a cone of energy that extends 30 feet from the palm of your hand. All creatures within the area must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes 4d6 lightning damage plus 1d6 lightning damage per target that failed the saving throw or half as much damage on a successful one.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 283 (Indie)

fields.name: Execution Blade (HB)
fields.text:
A blade of radiant light falls from the sky and hits a 5-foot radius area within range. Creatures in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, a creature takes 10d6 radiant damage that ignores any resistances and immunities, and the creature also has disadvantage on any ability checks it makes until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and does not suffer the additional effect.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 283 (Indie)

fields.name: Force Armor (HB)
fields.text:
An energy armor forms around you, changing your AC calculation to 12 + Dexterity modifier + Intelligence modifier. Your AC cannot be increased or reduced in any other way while this spell is active, whether by you, allies, enemies, or even items.
	If a creature within 60 feet deals damage to you, you can use your reaction to shatter the armor into several shards that turn into 4 darts and launch towards the creature that damaged you. Each of the darts deals 1d4+1 force damage to it. Doing so ends the spell.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the spell creates one more dart for each slot above 2nd when you use the reaction.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 283 (Indie)

fields.name: Force Arrow (HB)
fields.text:
You imbue magic into a ranged weapon that uses ammo, and when used by you, it fires magical ammo created on each attack, each ammo dealing in addition to its normal damage an extra 2d12 damage and all damage dealt is force damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 283 (Indie)

fields.name: Force of Hope (HB)
fields.text:
You encourage and give hope to all friendly creatures within range. For the duration, they gain 2d8 temporary hit points and a +2 bonus to their AC, attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 284 (Indie)

fields.name: Force of Salvation (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a diamond worth at least 100 gp, which the spell consumes)
fields.text:
You hold a diamond and make a circular motion with your arm, saying the name of your god, creating a light on up to three willing creatures that you can see within range. Each creature regains 5d8 hit points and the conditions caused by magical effects afflicting it are ended.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell with a spell slot of 8th level or higher, you affect one more creature per slot level above 7th.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 284 (Indie)

fields.name: Force Platform (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a jewel worth at least 20 gp)
fields.text:
You create eight cube-shaped platforms whose edge is 10 feet. You can position them as you wish, but at least one of them must be within 90 feet of you and they must all be connected to each other, with at least one of their sides necessarily touching the other of the cubes in order to connect them all. Each platform can hold up to 1000 pounds of load and the creatures can choose to walk on or walk through them. With a bonus action, you can move all of them up to 15 feet, rearranging them as you wish, while respecting the prerequisites mentioned above. Moving them this way causes creatures on top or inside of it to magically move this way. When the spell ends, all creatures on the platforms fall as usual.

At Higher Levels: If you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, you can create two more platforms for each slot level above 3rd.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 284 (Indie)

fields.name: Healing Breeze (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a mint leaf or similar herb)
fields.text:
You create a light and gentle breeze that rushes through the area relieving pain, effects and healing an ally. A creature of your choice within range recovers 4d6 hit points and reduces its exhaustion level by 1, if any.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 284 (Indie)

fields.name: Huradrin's Rune of Frost (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a small stone rune)
fields.text:
When you cast this spell, a glowing rune appears on the ground in a 5-foot square you can see within range. The first time a creature enters the area on a turn, or if it starts its turn there, it must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be frozen for the duration. A frozen creature takes 10d6 cold damage at the start of each of its turns and is petrified.
	The cold damage ignores resistance. At the end of each of its turns, the target can make another Constitution saving throw. On a success, it is no longer frozen. If a frozen creature starts its turn outside the area (for example, if an ally moves it away), this saving throw is made with advantage. If a frozen creature suffers the cold damage from this spell on 5 consecutive turns, it remains petrified after the spell ends.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 284 (Indie)

fields.name: Huradrin's Rune of Life (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a small rune carved from a gemstone worth at least 500 gp, which the spell consumes)
fields.text:
You target a dead creature within range, and a glowing rune appears on the ground in a 5-foot square that is under the dead body. If the creature's soul is free and willing, the creature returns to life with 10 hit point, provided that it has been dead no longer than 24 hours. This spell can't return a creature to life that has died of old age or one that is an undead, nor can it restore any missing body parts. If the creature is lacking body parts or organs integral for its survival—its head, for instance—the spell automatically fails.
	Each time the restored creature ends its turn in contact with the rune, it regains 10 hit points.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 284 (Indie)

fields.name: Huradrin's Rune of Stasis (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a small stone rune)
fields.text:
When you cast this spell, a glowing rune appears on the ground in a 5-foot square you can see within range. The first time a creature enters the area on a turn, or if it starts its turn there, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be paralyzed for the duration. At the end of each of its turns, the target can make another Wisdom saving throw. On a successful saving throw, it is no longer paralyzed. If the creature starts its turn outside the area (for example, if an ally moves it away), this saving throw is made with advantage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 284 (Indie)

fields.name: Huradrin's Rune of Storms (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a small stone rune)
fields.text:
When you cast this spell, a glowing rune appears on the ground in a 5-foot square you can see within range. The first time a creature enters the area on a turn, or if it starts its turn there, a bolt of lightning strikes the creature and it must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, it takes 5d6 lightning damage and is unable to take reactions until the start of its next turn.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 285 (Indie)

fields.name: Huradrin's Rune of Transformation (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a small stone rune)
fields.text:
When you cast this spell, a glowing rune appears on the ground in a 5-foot square you can see within range. The first time a creature touches the rune after the spell is cast, the rune disappears and a willing creature is transformed for the duration. An unwilling creature may make a Wisdom saving throw; on a success, the spell ends and the creature is not transformed. You choose which transformation occurs when the rune is touched: Reptilian, Avian or Botanic.

Reptilian: The target becomes covered in scales, grows a long tail, and its mouth turns into a crocodilian maw.

	• The maw is a natural weapon. The target can attack with it using your spell attack modifier, dealing piercing damage equal to 1d8 plus your spellcasting ability modifier on a hit.

	• The scaly hide provides improved protection. While the target is not wearing armor its AC is 13 plus your spellcasting ability modifier.

	• The tail has a reach of 10 feet. If a creature enters this reach, the target can take a reaction to attempt to trip the creature. Then, the creature must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC, or it falls prone.

Avian: The target becomes covered in feathers, grows wings, gains bird-like reflexes and hawk-like eyes.

	• The target gains a flying speed equal to its walking speed.
	• The target gains advantage on any perception checks based on sight.
	• When hit by an attack, the target may take a reaction to move up to its speed without provoking opportunity attacks.

Botanic: The target becomes covered in bark, and grows leaves and roots.

	• The target's speed becomes 0.
	• The target gains resistance to non-magical bludgeoning damage.
	• The target gains vulnerability to fire damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 285 (Indie)

fields.name: Inner Greed (HB)
fields.text:
You create a small illusory energy globe that transforms into the object or person most coveted by a chosen target, visible only to it. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, it becomes charmed by the object of its desire. While charmed by this spell, the creature is incapacitated and, on its turn, will move towards the illusion, regardless of any obstacles in its path.
	As a bonus action, you can move the globe up to 30 feet within the spell's range. The spell ends if another creature uses an action to shake the creature out of its stupor.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 285 (Indie)

fields.name: Locate Penumbral Portal (HB)
fields.text:
Component: V, S When casting this spell, you can feel the connections between this world and the Penumbral Plane, indicating where a nearby portal or rift to the Penumbral Plane may be located.
	You constantly sense the direction of the portal while it is within the spell's range.
	If you are playing outside of Tanares, you can find passages to the Shadowfell instead.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 285 (Indie)

fields.name: Longburrow's Comfortable Cottage (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a piece of bear skin)
fields.text:
When you cast this spell, a small cottage occupying a 20 foot square, with a height of 10 feet, appears in an unoccupied space on the ground within range. A small fire burns in the fireplace in the cottage, keeping the temperature at a comfortable level regardless of the weather outside. The cottage is made of wood, with a single door facing the caster, and one 5-foot square window adorning each side wall. The interior is furnished with 4 sets of bunk beds with comfortable bedding and a padded chair facing the fireplace. A pantry in the cottage and a barrel of ale in the corner contain enough ale and provisions to sustain 8 people for one day. At the end of the duration, the cottage and any remaining contents created by the spell vanish.
	For the duration, any creature that completes a long rest inside the cottage may reduce an extra level of exhaustion or remove a single condition afflicting it.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 285 (Indie)

fields.name: Longburrow's Cozy Campfire (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (some whipped sugar and gelatin)
fields.text:
You target a small non-magical campfire in range and magically transform it to be especially warm and inviting. Any creature that finishes a short rest within 30 feet of the fire while this spell is in effect may roll 2 dice for each Hit Die spent to recover hit points.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 286 (Indie)

fields.name: Longburrow's Homey Hearth (HB)
fields.text:
You target a fireplace within range and a warm and comforting fire erupts, which lasts for 8 hours. Any creature that completes a long rest in the same room of the fireplace while this spell is in effect regains all expended Hit Dice.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 286 (Indie)

fields.name: Melody of Nemesis (HB)
fields.text:
You play a haunting melody. Each creature other than you within range that can hear the tune must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature loses half of its current hit points, rounded down.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 286 (Indie)

fields.name: Memory Trial (HB)
fields.classes: School: Divination, Touch Spells, Bard, Ranger, Wizard
fields.text:
Upon touching an object, you gain insights from its past. There are two ways to use this spell:

	• Recent Memory: Upon casting, you can perceive everything that has transpired around the object since it settled in its current location. For the next hour, you can see and hear all events in the vicinity of the object, regardless of how long it has been in that position. Minor adjustments to the object's location, like being shifted during cleaning, don't disrupt the spell's effect.

	• Distant Memory: Alternatively, you can specify a particular moment within the past year. You then experience the same sensory effect as the first method.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 286 (Indie)

fields.name: Metal to Wood (HB)
fields.text:
You create a magical shock in a 20-foot cube within range, transmuting crafted objects made of metal into wood. Creatures within the area must make a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, all equipped and carried equipment made of metal is turned into wood. Objects and equipment that are not being equipped or carried are automatically transmuted. Nonmagical objects are transmuted permanently, while magic items are transformed for just 24 hours. Weapons transformed into wood are considered improvised weapons and have a -2 penalty to attack and damage rolls and transformed armors have a -3 penalty to their AC.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 286 (Indie)

fields.name: Mind Reshaping (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (between 100 and 1,000 gp of tameranium and bauronite equally divided, which the spell consumes)
fields.text:
In an elaborate ritual, you wipe clean the psyche of a humanoid creature and imprint a new directive, effectively making it almost irreversible. The targeted creature is required to be seated on an obsidian throne worth at least 5,000 gp atop a marble circle, both inscribed with arcane symbols. The creature must also be adorned with a tameranium bracelet on its right wrist and a bauronite bracelet on its left wrist.
	The spell carries significant side effects; however, these are mitigated by increasing amounts of tameranium and bauronite used. With a minimum of 50 gp worth of each material, you gain 2 levels of exhaustion and are unable to cast this spell for 48 hours. Utilizing at least 500 gp of each reduces the exhaustion to one level, but the spell remains unusable for 24 hours. If you use at least 1000 gp of each, you suffer no exhaustion but are unable to recast the spell for 12 hours. The spell fails if casted before the time above pass.
	The subject of the spell must remain seated for the entire casting time. Upon completion, you may choose to implement one of the directives Mindless Soldier, Berserker Beast, or Focused Servant on the target. The Mind Return option can be used on a target already affected by this spell to reverse its effects, which is the only way to do it besides the casting of a wish spell.

Mindless Soldier: The creature becomes dedicated to executing orders and will only comply with commands given by individuals bound to it during the casting. You can designate any number of entities that are part of the same organization known to the creature before the ritual.

Berserker Beast: The target operates on pure instinct and obeys only the caster's basic commands. The target loses speech capability and becomes exceptionally hostile. Also, it has advantage on Strength ability checks and saving throws, and it gains a +2 bonus on Strength-based damage rolls, while it has disadvantage on Intelligence ability checks and saving throws.

Focused Servant: The target concentrates all its proficiency on one particular field of knowledge. Choose one skill or tool. The creature gains proficiency in it, doubles its proficiency bonus for checks related to it, and gains advantage on these checks. However, it cannot apply its proficiency bonus to any other skill checks that aren't directly related to the chosen skill or tool.

Mind Return: For this effect, it is also necessary to provide an object that once belonged to the target, which the spell consumes. If done, you revert the target to its state before the spell was cast on it.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 287 (Indie)

fields.name: Nature Boon (HB)
Nightmare Hug (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a black pearl worth at least 100 gp)
fields.text:
You summon a shadowy shape behind the target creature that embraces it. The creature must make a Constitution saving throw. If it fails, it suffers 1d4 levels of exhaustion and its respective effects for the duration of the spell. If the creature reaches the sixth level of exhaustion, it does not die but is unconscious for 24 hours, only suffering from 5 levels of exhaustion that remain even after the spell's duration. An affected creature that hasn't suffered all 6 levels of exhaustion can make a new save at the end of its turns, getting rid of this spell's effects on a success.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 287 (Indie)

fields.name: Notes of Biot (HB)
fields.text:
You conjure powerful notes that echo in a 60-foot radius sphere from a point within the spell's range. Hostile creatures that enter or start their turn in the area take 8d8 thunder damage and must make a Constitution saving throw. On a success, a creature takes only half as much damage. On a failure, a creature also must roll 1d8 to define which note ran through its body and which condition affected it, according to the following table. The condition lasts for 1 minute, and the affected creature can redo the save at the end of its turns, ending the condition on a success. If a creature receives more than one condition from this spell, it makes a single saving throw at the end of its turns, ending all conditions that have affected it on a success.

Notes of Biot:
Dice | Note | Effect
1 | Do | The creature is Paralyzed
2 | Re | The creature is Charmed
3 | Mi | The creature is Stunned
4 | Fa | The creature is Restrained
5 | Sol | The creature is unable to speak or utter other sounds
6 | La | The creature is Blinded
7 | Si | The creature is Frightened
8 | Chord | +4d8 thunder damage and roll again on the table.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 287 (Indie)

fields.name: Offer (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (8 sp in incenses, which the spell consumes)
fields.text:
You make an offering to your god, asking him for guidance on the day ahead. For the next 24 hours, anytime you roll a d20 to determine the outcome of any action, you can choose to roll an additional d20 and choose which of the two results to use. You can declare you are using the extra d20 either before or after you make the first roll, but always before the GM declares the outcome. Once you use the roll the spell ends and can't be used again before the next dawn.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 288 (Indie)

fields.name: Penumbral Fissure (HB)
fields.text:
The caster opens a fissure of up to 60 square feet between the Material Plane and the Penumbral Plane to the fissure, allowing creatures to cross from one plane to the correspondent place in the other. Alternatively, you can close an existing fissure between these planes, as long as it does not exceed 60 square feet. A fissure created by this spell automatically closes if a penumbral creature comes within 5 feet of it, but reopens when there are no penumbral creatures within that range.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 288 (Indie)

fields.name: Phantom Vision (HB)
fields.classes: School: Divination, Touch Spells, Bard, Ranger, Wizard
fields.text:
You touch the target's eyes and they become yellow, allowing it to see creatures through solid objects, such as walls. For the duration, the target can see creatures, not objects, within a range of 20 feet through any obstacle up to 2 feet thick, regardless of the lack of light in the area. In darkness, the image of the creature is not sharp and its colors become only shades of red.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 288 (Indie)

fields.name: Prayer of the Desperates (HB)
fields.text:
You make a prayer asking your god to protect the desperate and heal the wounded.
	Choose up to three creatures within range to regain 1d6 hit points. In addition, if the creature had 0 hit points, it receives +2 to its AC until the start of its next turn, and can immediately choose to take a reaction to stand up from prone.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 288 (Indie)

fields.name: Pressure Empowerment (HB)
fields.text:
Upon casting this spell, the magic propels a piece of ammunition from your hand, in a grand arc towards a target, exerting immense pressure as it descends. Make a ranged spell attack. On a hit, the target takes 8d6 force damage and is knocked prone. On a miss, the creature takes half as much damage and must make a saving throw, choosing between Strength or Dexterity, to avoid being knocked prone.
	Any other creature within 20 feet of the target must make a Strength or Dexterity saving throw (creature's choice). On a failure, the creature takes 8d6 force damage and is knocked prone. On a success, it takes half as much damage and is not knocked prone. Creatures of Large size or larger have advantage on the saving throw.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 288 (Indie)

fields.name: Pure Light Slash (HB)
fields.text:
You conjure an immense blade of pure luminescence overhead, which descends and morphs into one of the forms you select:

	• A sweeping slash in a 15-foot cone in front of you, inflicting 3d4 radiant damage to all creatures within the area.

	• A powerful thrust directly in front of you, causing 3d4 radiant damage to all creatures within its trajectory in a 25-foot line.

	• Several shards of brilliant light, dealing 3d4 radiant damage to all creatures adjacent to you.

All creatures within the area must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking half as much damage on a success.

At Higher Levels: Casting this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher amplifies the damage by an additional 1d4 for each slot level above 1st.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 288 (Indie)

fields.name: Purge (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a diamond worth at least 2000 gp that has been blessed by a cleric, which is consumed by the spell)
fields.text:
You call down a beam of holy light to smite an enemy. The creature must succeed on a Charisma saving throw, taking 10d8 radiant damage plus 10d8 fire damage, is permanently blinded and becomes afflicted with the effects of the slow spell for a minute on a failure. On a success, it takes half as much damage, is blinded for 1 minute and is not slowed. If the target is native to a different plane of existence than the one you're on, he has disadvantage on the saving throw. A permanently blinded creature can only remove the condition by the spells greater restoration, regeneration, wish, or similar abilities.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 289 (Indie)

fields.name: Ray of Fear (HB)
fields.text:
You shoot a powerful beam of dark purple energy from your open hands at a creature within range. You make a ranged spell attack against the target, and if it hits, it takes 7d6 psychic damage and becomes frightened for 1d4 rounds.
	If you are in dim light or darkness, increase the damage by 3d6 and the target remains frightened for 2d4 rounds. The target can make a Wisdom saving throw at the end of each of its turns to end the frightened condition.

Frightened:
	• A frightened creature has disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls while the source of its fear is within line of sight.
	• The creature can't willingly move closer to the source of its fear.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 289 (Indie)

fields.name: Reveal Hidden Steps (HB)
fields.text:
As an action, you exhale a luminous magical breath that reveals the tracks of passing creatures within 30 feet of you. For the duration of the spell, you gain a +10 bonus on Wisdom (Survival) checks to track creatures.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 289 (Indie)

fields.name: Rurik's Energy Shield (HB)
fields.classes: School: Evocation, Paladin, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard
fields.text:
You create a large shield of energy embellished with dwarven runes, which revolves around you and provides three-quarters of cover. Any creature that makes a melee attack against you takes 5d6 force damage. As a bonus action, you can transform the barrier made by the shield into a handaxe of arcane energy, which forms in your hand. You can make a ranged spell attack with the axe as an action against a creature within 60 feet of you. On a hit, the attack deals 5d6 force damage, and if the target is larger than you, it must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or be knocked prone. For the duration, you can switch between the axe and the shield forms as a bonus action. If you take any damage, the spell ends.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 289 (Indie)

fields.name: Shadow Noose (HB)
fields.classes: Cleric (Chaos Domain (Tanares) (HB)), School: Necromancy, Druid, Ranger, Warlock
fields.text:
Upon casting this spell, beams of necrotic energy burst from the shadow of a target creature within range, seeking to ensnare it. The target creature must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, shadowy tendrils form around the creature for the duration of the spell, halving its speed and inflicting necrotic damage equal to 1d6 plus your spellcasting ability modifier.
	The ensnared creature may attempt a new saving throw at the end of each of its turns to free itself. Until it succeeds, it suffers necrotic damage equal to 1d6 plus your spellcasting ability modifier at the beginning of each of its turns. On a successful save, the spell ends.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 289 (Indie)

fields.name: Shadow Sword (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a onyx gem worth at least 25 gp, which the spell consumes)
fields.text:
You choose a target that you can see within the spell's range and create a sword of negative energy, which emerges from the target's shadow and attacks. Make a melee spell attack against the target. On a hit, the sword stabs the creature, dealing 5d10 necrotic damage. The sword remains stuck to the target, and on subsequent turns, you can use your action to deal 4d10 necrotic damage to the target automatically. The sword dissipates and the spell ends if you use your action to do anything else.
	The creature cannot have its hit points restored by any means until the sword is removed or the spell ends. A creature can attempt to remove the sword using its action to make a Charisma saving throw. On a success, the sword is removed, the target takes 5d10 necrotic damage, and the spell ends. On a failure, the sword is not removed, and the target takes half as much damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 289 (Indie)

fields.name: Shield of Light (HB)
fields.text:
You manifest a radiant energy barrier that you can wield. For all purposes, it functions as a shield, but allows the execution of somatic components to cast spells.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the barrier becomes a +1 shield. When you use a spell slot of 5th level or higher, the bonus increases to +2, and, when you use a spell slot of 8th level or higher, the bonus increases to +3.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 290 (Indie)
